🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #26 of 30 (18 NOV)

📰 Centre offers up to 75% relief in environmental compensation to groundwater users

📌 Published: 18 Nov 2026, 04:29:18 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: One-time settlement scheme offers 30-75% relief on groundwater environmental compensation to regulate, regularise, and settle disputes across projects in 19 States and Union Territories

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The government has introduced a one-time settlement scheme offering 30 to 75% relief in environmental compensation imposed on industries, infrastructure projects, mining units and other groundwater users for extracting the resource without mandatory permissions, delayed renewal of permits or extracting it beyond the permitted limit. The Ground Water Charges (Dispute Resolution) Scheme, 2026, notified by the Ministry of Jal Shakti on November 12, aims to encourage project proponents to regularise groundwater extraction, bring more users into the regulatory framework and facilitate settlement of disputes and pending litigation over environmental compensation. The scheme will remain in force for one year from the date of its publication in the official gazette and will cover projects in 19 States and Union Territories where groundwater regulation is being carried out by the Central Ground Water Authority (CGWA). According to the notification, the scheme has been conceived as a “voluntary, one-time strategic resolution and settlement mechanism” with the primary objective of achieving wider regulatory compliance. The notification said substantial environmental compensation liabilities had discouraged several project proponents from voluntarily entering the regulatory framework, while a significant number of cases remained entangled in prolonged representations and litigation, delaying recovery of compensation. The scheme provides relief in three categories of violations — existing projects extracting groundwater without a valid No Objection Certificate (NOC), projects applying late for renewal of NOCs and projects extracting groundwater beyond the quantity permitted under their NOCs. The maximum relief of 75% will be available to projects that have extracted groundwater in excess of the permitted quantity, while those applying late for renewal of NOCs can get relief ranging from 40 to 70%. Projects operating without NOCs will be eligible for 30 to 60% relief. The extent of relief will depend on the groundwater assessment category of the area and the quantity of groundwater extracted by a project. The notification classifies assessment units into five categories — safe, semi-critical, critical, over-exploited and saline — and prescribes different rates of concessions based on groundwater consumption slabs of less than 200 kilolitres per day (KLD), 200 to less than 1,000 KLD, 1,000 to less than 5,000 KLD and 5,000 KLD or above.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: For existing projects operating without NOCs, the relief will range from 60% in safe and saline assessment units to 30% in over-exploited areas for projects extracting 5,000 KLD or more.

📚 TOP 4 HARD VOCABULARY WORDS EXTRACTED FROM THIS PARAGRAPH (TAP CARD FOR PICTURE & SYNONYMS):
Quantitative (Adjective)
आंकड़ों और संख्या पर आधारित — जिसे ठोस नंबरों और डेटा में मापा जा सके।
✓ Syn: Measurable, Numerical, Empirical  |  ✖ Ant: Qualitative, Subjective, Unmeasurable
Environmental (Adjective)
पर्यावरण, प्रकृति और हमारे पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र (Ecosystem) से संबंधित।
✓ Syn: Ecological, Biospheric, Natural  |  ✖ Ant: Industrial, Polluting, Synthetic
Permissibility (Noun)
कानूनी अनुमति या स्वीकार्यता — किसी कार्य को करने की वैध छूट।
✓ Syn: Admissibility, Legality, Allowance  |  ✖ Ant: Prohibition, Ban, Illegality
Compensation (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Compensation' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial

D. The author contends that 'Centre offers up to 75% relief in environment' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. articles.title: Xiaomi 18 Pro and Xiaomi 18 Pro Max launched with a back display
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The Xiaomi 18 Pro series continues to bring Leica-tuned lenses in the flagship phones, while running on the latest chipsets from Qualcomm

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Xiaomi has launched its new flagship smartphones, the Xiaomi 18 Pro and Xiaomi 18 Pro Max , in a global unveil. The Xiaomi 18 Pro series features a back display that can be used to view notification and can also act as a viewfinder. The Xiaomi 18 Pro series continues to bring Leica-tuned lenses in the flagship phones, while running on the latest chipsets from Qualcomm. Xiaomi 18 Pro Max has a 6.9 inch LTPO AMOLED display with a dynamic refresh rate up to 120 Hz, 4,000 nits peak brightness, supporting Dolby Vision and HDR10+. The Xiaomi 18 Pro gets a 6.4 inch display with similar refresh rate and brightness. Xiaomi has also introduced a privacy mode like Samsung, which reduces pixels brightness if viewed from sides to avoid glancing. It can be applied to selected apps, notifications, floating windows, and split-screen views. The back display has up to 4,000 nits peak brightness with a 1-120 Hz LTPO refresh rate, protected by Corning Gorilla Glass Victus 2. It can also be used as a real-time translation tool that displays each speaker’s language on their respective side for face-to-face communication in 29 languages. Xiaomi 18 Pro Max runs on the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6, while Xiaomi 18 Pro features the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 SoC. Xiaomi 18 Pro series operates on HyperOS 4 based on Android 17 out of the box. Xiaomi 18 Pro Max ships with a 7,050 mAh battery with 100W wired and 50W wireless HyperCharge; Xiaomi 18 Pro gets a 6,000 mAh battery with 90W wired and 50W wireless HyperCharge. Both, Xiaomi 18 Pro Max and Xiaomi 18 Pro sport a 200 MP main camera, a 200 MP telephoto lens, a 50 MP ultrawide sensor, along with a 50 MP selfie camera. Xiaomi 18 Pro Max starts at €1,599, while Xiaomi 18 Pro begins at €1,399. The series is available in Black, White, Cosmic Blue, and Velvet Red.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: technology (general) / gadgets (general) / PDAs and smartphones / camera mobiles

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #27 of 30 (18 NOV)

📰 Xiaomi 18 Pro and Xiaomi 18 Pro Max launched with a back display

📌 Published: 18 Nov 2026, 03:32:07 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The Xiaomi 18 Pro series continues to bring Leica-tuned lenses in the flagship phones, while running on the latest chipsets from Qualcomm

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Xiaomi has launched its new flagship smartphones, the Xiaomi 18 Pro and Xiaomi 18 Pro Max , in a global unveil. The Xiaomi 18 Pro series features a back display that can be used to view notification and can also act as a viewfinder. The Xiaomi 18 Pro series continues to bring Leica-tuned lenses in the flagship phones, while running on the latest chipsets from Qualcomm. Xiaomi 18 Pro Max has a 6.9 inch LTPO AMOLED display with a dynamic refresh rate up to 120 Hz, 4,000 nits peak brightness, supporting Dolby Vision and HDR10+. The Xiaomi 18 Pro gets a 6.4 inch display with similar refresh rate and brightness. Xiaomi has also introduced a privacy mode like Samsung, which reduces pixels brightness if viewed from sides to avoid glancing. It can be applied to selected apps, notifications, floating windows, and split-screen views. The back display has up to 4,000 nits peak brightness with a 1-120 Hz LTPO refresh rate, protected by Corning Gorilla Glass Victus 2. It can also be used as a real-time translation tool that displays each speaker’s language on their respective side for face-to-face communication in 29 languages. Xiaomi 18 Pro Max runs on the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6, while Xiaomi 18 Pro features the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 SoC. Xiaomi 18 Pro series operates on HyperOS 4 based on Android 17 out of the box. Xiaomi 18 Pro Max ships with a 7,050 mAh battery with 100W wired and 50W wireless HyperCharge; Xiaomi 18 Pro gets a 6,000 mAh battery with 90W wired and 50W wireless HyperCharge. Both, Xiaomi 18 Pro Max and Xiaomi 18 Pro sport a 200 MP main camera, a 200 MP telephoto lens, a 50 MP ultrawide sensor, along with a 50 MP selfie camera. Xiaomi 18 Pro Max starts at €1,599, while Xiaomi 18 Pro begins at €1,399. The series is available in Black, White, Cosmic Blue, and Velvet Red.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: technology (general) / gadgets (general) / PDAs and smartphones / camera mobiles

articles.title: R. Ashok challenges Karnataka govt. to hold local body polls instead of blaming Centre
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Leader of the Opposition in the Legislative Assembly, R. Ashok, on Wednesday accused the Congress government of “financial mismanagement” and challenged it to conduct elections to local bodies instead of blaming the Centre for the alleged delay in releasing grants.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Addressing a press conference, he alleged that the State government had failed to transfer about ₹225 crore of the grants released by the Centre to gram panchayats in 2024-25 and was attempting to shift the blame to the Union government. “The Centre had released ₹2,133.25 crore for the development of Gram Panchayats during 2024-25, but the State government had transferred only ₹1,907 crore,” he claimed. Read | Karnataka to move Supreme Court over ₹2,186 crore rural development grants: Eshwar Khandre As per the rules, the State government is required to transfer the funds to gram panchayats within 10 days of their release by the Centre. This provision was introduced during the previous Congress-led UPA government, but the present Congress government was not adhering to it, he alleged. Mr. Ashok said the State government should stop confronting the Centre and instead work in coordination with it for the development of Karnataka. He alleged that Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar was continuing the confrontational approach adopted by Siddaramaiah during his previous tenure as Chief Minister. Mr. Ashok also questioned the State government’s continued postponement of elections to zilla and taluk panchayats, pointing out that conducting local body elections was among the conditions for the release of grants. The government should hold the elections and make public a detailed account of the funds received from the Centre and transferred to gram panchayats, he demanded. The delay in transferring funds had affected basic amenities in rural areas, including drinking water supply, street lighting, drainage and sanitation, he alleged. He further stated that the government had failed to fulfil several promises made to farmers, pensioners, ASHAs and anganwadi workers.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Mr. Ashok alleged that the government had initially announced ₹2,500 as drought relief for farmers and subsequently increased it to ₹5,000, but only ₹1,000 or ₹1,500 was being credited to beneficiaries’ accounts. Citing technical glitches to justify the shortfall was unacceptable, particularly in a State known for its IT sector, he said.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #7 of 30 (18 NOV)

📰 R. Ashok challenges Karnataka govt. to hold local body polls instead of blaming Centre

📌 Published: 18 Nov 2026, 07:29:56 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Leader of the Opposition in the Legislative Assembly, R. Ashok, on Wednesday accused the Congress government of “financial mismanagement” and challenged it to conduct elections to local bodies instead of blaming the Centre for the alleged delay in releasing grants.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Addressing a press conference, he alleged that the State government had failed to transfer about ₹225 crore of the grants released by the Centre to gram panchayats in 2024-25 and was attempting to shift the blame to the Union government. “The Centre had released ₹2,133.25 crore for the development of Gram Panchayats during 2024-25, but the State government had transferred only ₹1,907 crore,” he claimed. Read | Karnataka to move Supreme Court over ₹2,186 crore rural development grants: Eshwar Khandre As per the rules, the State government is required to transfer the funds to gram panchayats within 10 days of their release by the Centre. This provision was introduced during the previous Congress-led UPA government, but the present Congress government was not adhering to it, he alleged. Mr. Ashok said the State government should stop confronting the Centre and instead work in coordination with it for the development of Karnataka. He alleged that Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar was continuing the confrontational approach adopted by Siddaramaiah during his previous tenure as Chief Minister. Mr. Ashok also questioned the State government’s continued postponement of elections to zilla and taluk panchayats, pointing out that conducting local body elections was among the conditions for the release of grants. The government should hold the elections and make public a detailed account of the funds received from the Centre and transferred to gram panchayats, he demanded. The delay in transferring funds had affected basic amenities in rural areas, including drinking water supply, street lighting, drainage and sanitation, he alleged. He further stated that the government had failed to fulfil several promises made to farmers, pensioners, ASHAs and anganwadi workers.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Mr. Ashok alleged that the government had initially announced ₹2,500 as drought relief for farmers and subsequently increased it to ₹5,000, but only ₹1,000 or ₹1,500 was being credited to beneficiaries’ accounts. Citing technical glitches to justify the shortfall was unacceptable, particularly in a State known for its IT sector, he said.

✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Coordination (Noun)
समन्वय — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Coordination' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।

articles.keyPoints:
• 1. Core Context & Background: Leader of the Opposition in the Legislative Assembly, R. Ashok, on Wednesday accused the Congress government of “financial mismanagement” and challenged it to conduct elections to local bodies instead of blaming the Centre for the alleged delay in releasing grants.
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Addressing a press conference, he alleged that the State government had failed to transfer about ₹225 crore of the grants released by the Centre to gram panchayats in 2024-25 and was attempting to shift the blame to the Union government. “The Centre had released ₹2,133.25 crore for the development of Gram Panchayats during 2024-25, but the State government had transferred only ₹1,907 crore,” he claimed. Read | Karnataka to move Supreme Court over ₹2,186 crore rural development grants: Eshwar Khandre As per the rules, the State government is required to transfer the funds to gram panchayats within 10 days of their release by the Centre. This provision was introduced during the previous Congress-led UPA government, but the present Congress government was not adhering to it, he alleged. Mr. Ashok said the State government should stop confronting the Centre and instead work in coordination with it for the development of Karnataka. He alleged that Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar was continuing the confrontational approach adopted by Siddaramaiah during his previous tenure as Chief Minister. Mr. Ashok also questioned the State government’s continued postponement of elections to zilla and taluk panchayats, pointing out that conducting local body elections was among the conditions for the release of grants. The government should hold the elections and make public a detailed account of the funds received from the Centre and transferred to gram panchayats, he demanded. The delay in transferring funds had affected basic amenities in rural areas, including drinking water supply, street lighting, drainage and sanitation, he alleged. He further stated that the government had failed to fulfil several promises made to farmers, pensioners, ASHAs and anganwadi workers.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Mr. Ashok alleged that the government had initially announced ₹2,500 as drought relief for farmers and subsequently increased it to ₹5,000, but only ₹1,000 or ₹1,500 was being credited to beneficiaries’ accounts. Citing technical glitches to justify the shortfall was unacceptable, particularly in a State known for its IT sector, he said.

articles.title: Premature babies can grow healthy with proper medical care, family support, says expert
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Addressing a event held to mark World Prematurity Day, Dr. Govardhan Reddy, KIMS Cuddles senior consultant paediatrician, says it was heartening to see children who were born prematurely, overcoming several health challenges and now growing up to become healthy and active

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Babies born prematurely can grow up healthy and lead normal lives with timely medical intervention, advanced neonatal intensive care, appropriate nutrition, parental involvement and regular medical follow-up, said Dr. Govardhan Reddy, senior consultant paediatrician at KIMS Cuddles. To mark World Prematurity Day, KIMS Cuddles, Kurnool, organised a special programme bringing together children who were born prematurely at KIMS Hospitals over the past seven years and received specialised medical care, along with their parents and family members. Speaking on the occasion, Dr. Govardhan Reddy said it was heartening to see children who were born prematurely, overcoming several health challenges and now growing up to become healthy and active. He said that with appropriate medical care and family support, premature babies could grow just like other children and excel in academics and other fields. Their progress and achievements also provide confidence and reassurance to parents of other premature babies. The programme also aimed to create awareness about the health challenges faced by babies born prematurely and the specialised medical care and continued monitoring they require.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: A range of entertaining activities, including songs, dance performances and a fashion show, was organised for the children. Parents of premature babies had an opportunity to interact with one another, share their experiences and celebrate their children’s growth and achievements.

📰 Premature babies can grow healthy with proper medical care, family support, says expert

📌 Published: 18 Nov 2026, 07:28:04 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Addressing a event held to mark World Prematurity Day, Dr. Govardhan Reddy, KIMS Cuddles senior consultant paediatrician, says it was heartening to see children who were born prematurely, overcoming several health challenges and now growing up to become healthy and active

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Babies born prematurely can grow up healthy and lead normal lives with timely medical intervention, advanced neonatal intensive care, appropriate nutrition, parental involvement and regular medical follow-up, said Dr. Govardhan Reddy, senior consultant paediatrician at KIMS Cuddles. To mark World Prematurity Day, KIMS Cuddles, Kurnool, organised a special programme bringing together children who were born prematurely at KIMS Hospitals over the past seven years and received specialised medical care, along with their parents and family members. Speaking on the occasion, Dr. Govardhan Reddy said it was heartening to see children who were born prematurely, overcoming several health challenges and now growing up to become healthy and active. He said that with appropriate medical care and family support, premature babies could grow just like other children and excel in academics and other fields. Their progress and achievements also provide confidence and reassurance to parents of other premature babies. The programme also aimed to create awareness about the health challenges faced by babies born prematurely and the specialised medical care and continued monitoring they require.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: A range of entertaining activities, including songs, dance performances and a fashion show, was organised for the children. Parents of premature babies had an opportunity to interact with one another, share their experiences and celebrate their children’s growth and achievements.

articles.title: Micro units in Coimbatore hit because of freezing of accounts by Commercial Taxes Department
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Puviarasu, a micro industry owner in Coimbatore city, operates four CNC machines, taking up job orders for companies in Kerala, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu. In 2017, when the Central government introduced Goods and Services Tax (GST), he had not paid the duty for six months. He got a waiver from penalty and interest for this through an amnesty scheme that the Centre introduced and paid the GST amount on the portal. Since then, he is paying GST every month and it goes up to ₹1.5 lakh a month.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: In 2022, Mr. Puviarasu got a notice from the Commercial Taxes Department of Tamil Nadu, asking him to pay the penalty and interest for 2017. He replied to the notice citing the amnesty scheme. Three months ago, he was notified on the GST portal that he had to pay ₹88,000 as penalty and interest arrears and his current account was frozen. His savings accounts linked to his PAN were also frozen. “I borrowed ₹6 lakh from a private lender to pay Deepavali bonus for workers. I am paying just ₹12,000 as GST now because my company’s current account is frozen and I am unable to buy raw materials,” he told The Hindu on Wednesday (November 18, 2026). Maniraj, another micro entrepreneur, got a similar notice for ₹30,000 and his account was frozen. He paid the amount and is waiting for a letter from the GST office so that his company’s bank account can be operated again. “I cannot fight the Commercial Taxes Department and I need to run the business. So, I paid the amount,” he said. Prabhakaran, who runs two units that have an annual turnover of ₹1.5 crore each, faces a different problem. One of the companies that was supplying materials to him was closed last financial year. He had claimed input tax credit for his transactions with that company. The Commercial Taxes Department asked him to repay the input tax credit, which he did. He was asked to pay the amount again and his account was frozen. When he took up the issue with the Department, he was told that it was a mistake and his account will be operational. Yet, the issue has not been addressed. “My customers are unable to pay me because my account is frozen,” he said. These are a few instances of the GST issues that the micro industries, numbering over 25,000, in Coimbatore district are facing for the last couple of years. To make things worse, freezing of current accounts has increased now affecting the businesses. “The official at the Department told me that I can go to court or pay the amount. They told me that every one was paying the amount and I should not raise the issue,” claims Mr. Puviarasu. C. Sivakumar, president of the Coimbatore Tirupur District Tiny and Micro Enterprises Association, says the Association has submitted to the Department details of the members affected. “We have sent petitions to the Chief Minister and the Commercial Taxes Minister requesting relief for all those who had made use of the Central government’s amnesty scheme in 2019, 2020, and 2021. Freezing of accounts, not addressing the issue when it is raised with the officials, and forcing the micro units to pay penalty or interest for GST issues resolved five years ago and issuing notices under section 74 indicating that the units have done fraudulent activities have hit the micro units badly. Many of them were forced to borrow funds at high interest rates from private lenders for Deepavali. The government should look into this issue urgently and address it,” he said.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Coimbatore / Tamil Nadu / taxes and duties / industrial production

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #10 of 30 (18 NOV)

📰 Micro units in Coimbatore hit because of freezing of accounts by Commercial Taxes Department

📌 Published: 18 Nov 2026, 07:26:55 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Puviarasu, a micro industry owner in Coimbatore city, operates four CNC machines, taking up job orders for companies in Kerala, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu. In 2017, when the Central government introduced Goods and Services Tax (GST), he had not paid the duty for six months. He got a waiver from penalty and interest for this through an amnesty scheme that the Centre introduced and paid the GST amount on the portal. Since then, he is paying GST every month and it goes up to ₹1.5 lakh a month.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: In 2022, Mr. Puviarasu got a notice from the Commercial Taxes Department of Tamil Nadu, asking him to pay the penalty and interest for 2017. He replied to the notice citing the amnesty scheme. Three months ago, he was notified on the GST portal that he had to pay ₹88,000 as penalty and interest arrears and his current account was frozen. His savings accounts linked to his PAN were also frozen. “I borrowed ₹6 lakh from a private lender to pay Deepavali bonus for workers. I am paying just ₹12,000 as GST now because my company’s current account is frozen and I am unable to buy raw materials,” he told The Hindu on Wednesday (November 18, 2026). Maniraj, another micro entrepreneur, got a similar notice for ₹30,000 and his account was frozen. He paid the amount and is waiting for a letter from the GST office so that his company’s bank account can be operated again. “I cannot fight the Commercial Taxes Department and I need to run the business. So, I paid the amount,” he said. Prabhakaran, who runs two units that have an annual turnover of ₹1.5 crore each, faces a different problem. One of the companies that was supplying materials to him was closed last financial year. He had claimed input tax credit for his transactions with that company. The Commercial Taxes Department asked him to repay the input tax credit, which he did. He was asked to pay the amount again and his account was frozen. When he took up the issue with the Department, he was told that it was a mistake and his account will be operational. Yet, the issue has not been addressed. “My customers are unable to pay me because my account is frozen,” he said. These are a few instances of the GST issues that the micro industries, numbering over 25,000, in Coimbatore district are facing for the last couple of years. To make things worse, freezing of current accounts has increased now affecting the businesses. “The official at the Department told me that I can go to court or pay the amount. They told me that every one was paying the amount and I should not raise the issue,” claims Mr. Puviarasu. C. Sivakumar, president of the Coimbatore Tirupur District Tiny and Micro Enterprises Association, says the Association has submitted to the Department details of the members affected. “We have sent petitions to the Chief Minister and the Commercial Taxes Minister requesting relief for all those who had made use of the Central government’s amnesty scheme in 2019, 2020, and 2021. Freezing of accounts, not addressing the issue when it is raised with the officials, and forcing the micro units to pay penalty or interest for GST issues resolved five years ago and issuing notices under section 74 indicating that the units have done fraudulent activities have hit the micro units badly. Many of them were forced to borrow funds at high interest rates from private lenders for Deepavali. The government should look into this issue urgently and address it,” he said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Coimbatore / Tamil Nadu / taxes and duties / industrial production

articles.keyPoints:
• 1. Core Context & Background: Puviarasu, a micro industry owner in Coimbatore city, operates four CNC machines, taking up job orders for companies in Kerala, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu. In 2017, when the Central government introduced Goods and Services Tax (GST), he had not paid the duty for six months. He got a waiver from penalty and interest for this through an amnesty scheme that the Centre introduced and paid the GST amount on the portal. Since then, he is paying GST every month and it goes up to ₹1.5 lakh a month.
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: In 2022, Mr. Puviarasu got a notice from the Commercial Taxes Department of Tamil Nadu, asking him to pay the penalty and interest for 2017. He replied to the notice citing the amnesty scheme. Three months ago, he was notified on the GST portal that he had to pay ₹88,000 as penalty and interest arrears and his current account was frozen. His savings accounts linked to his PAN were also frozen. “I borrowed ₹6 lakh from a private lender to pay Deepavali bonus for workers. I am paying just ₹12,000 as GST now because my company’s current account is frozen and I am unable to buy raw materials,” he told The Hindu on Wednesday (November 18, 2026). Maniraj, another micro entrepreneur, got a similar notice for ₹30,000 and his account was frozen. He paid the amount and is waiting for a letter from the GST office so that his company’s bank account can be operated again. “I cannot fight the Commercial Taxes Department and I need to run the business. So, I paid the amount,” he said. Prabhakaran, who runs two units that have an annual turnover of ₹1.5 crore each, faces a different problem. One of the companies that was supplying materials to him was closed last financial year. He had claimed input tax credit for his transactions with that company. The Commercial Taxes Department asked him to repay the input tax credit, which he did. He was asked to pay the amount again and his account was frozen. When he took up the issue with the Department, he was told that it was a mistake and his account will be operational. Yet, the issue has not been addressed. “My customers are unable to pay me because my account is frozen,” he said. These are a few instances of the GST issues that the micro industries, numbering over 25,000, in Coimbatore district are facing for the last couple of years. To make things worse, freezing of current accounts has increased now affecting the businesses. “The official at the Department told me that I can go to court or pay the amount. They told me that every one was paying the amount and I should not raise the issue,” claims Mr. Puviarasu. C. Sivakumar, president of the Coimbatore Tirupur District Tiny and Micro Enterprises Association, says the Association has submitted to the Department details of the members affected. “We have sent petitions to the Chief Minister and the Commercial Taxes Minister requesting relief for all those who had made use of the Central government’s amnesty scheme in 2019, 2020, and 2021. Freezing of accounts, not addressing the issue when it is raised with the officials, and forcing the micro units to pay penalty or interest for GST issues resolved five years ago and issuing notices under section 74 indicating that the units have done fraudulent activities have hit the micro units badly. Many of them were forced to borrow funds at high interest rates from private lenders for Deepavali. The government should look into this issue urgently and address it,” he said.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Coimbatore / Tamil Nadu / taxes and duties / industrial production

articles.title: Language fest showcases culture of tribes
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: A three-day Janjatiya Bhasha Utsava (Tribal Language Festival), organised as part of the Janjatiya Gaurav Divas celebrations honouring tribal freedom fighter Birsa Munda, is under way at the Central Institute of Indian Languages (CIIL) in Mysuru.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Inaugurating the festival on Wednesday, Padma Shri awardee and Santhali writer Damayanti Beshra emphasised that India was a country of languages and that language was the soul of a community. It must be nurtured through traditions, songs, stories, customs, practices, festivals and celebrations, she said. Paying tribute to Birsa Munda, Ms. Beshra said his contribution to tribal identity and unity would remain unforgettable. His legacy had brought tribal communities together on a common platform, she said. Belonging to Odisha, a State that is home to 64 tribal communities, Ms. Beshra observed that language was much more than a means of communication, as it carried a community’s history, folklore, songs, customs and festivals. She emphasised that documentation alone was not sufficient and urged researchers to engage with tribal communities to understand their languages and cultural backgrounds. Chandra Bhushan Sharma, Vice-Chancellor of Vinoba Bhave University, called upon researchers to study tribal languages in the context of their culture, history and way of life. He stressed the need for research on tribal art, architecture, textiles, traditional medicine, food and ecological knowledge. Citing his research on the Koracha community of Karnataka, CIIL director Basavaraja Kodagunti explained the unique mathematical expressions preserved in its language, demonstrating the knowledge embedded in indigenous linguistic traditions. As part of the three-day festival, discussions will be held on a National Atlas of Tribal Languages, technology for low-resource languages, and the role of government policies and institutions in strengthening the indigenous language ecosystem. A tribal heritage exhibition organised as part of the festival showcases the everyday cultural life of the Toda, Munda, Soliga, Alu Kurumba, Sora, Gondi and Ulladan communities.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: A live demonstration of Munda Mundua painting by tribal artists was held on Wednesday. Alu Kurumba art will be displayed on Thursday, while Sora painting will be showcased on Friday.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #12 of 30 (18 NOV)

📰 Language fest showcases culture of tribes

📌 Published: 18 Nov 2026, 07:24:50 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: A three-day Janjatiya Bhasha Utsava (Tribal Language Festival), organised as part of the Janjatiya Gaurav Divas celebrations honouring tribal freedom fighter Birsa Munda, is under way at the Central Institute of Indian Languages (CIIL) in Mysuru.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Inaugurating the festival on Wednesday, Padma Shri awardee and Santhali writer Damayanti Beshra emphasised that India was a country of languages and that language was the soul of a community. It must be nurtured through traditions, songs, stories, customs, practices, festivals and celebrations, she said. Paying tribute to Birsa Munda, Ms. Beshra said his contribution to tribal identity and unity would remain unforgettable. His legacy had brought tribal communities together on a common platform, she said. Belonging to Odisha, a State that is home to 64 tribal communities, Ms. Beshra observed that language was much more than a means of communication, as it carried a community’s history, folklore, songs, customs and festivals. She emphasised that documentation alone was not sufficient and urged researchers to engage with tribal communities to understand their languages and cultural backgrounds. Chandra Bhushan Sharma, Vice-Chancellor of Vinoba Bhave University, called upon researchers to study tribal languages in the context of their culture, history and way of life. He stressed the need for research on tribal art, architecture, textiles, traditional medicine, food and ecological knowledge. Citing his research on the Koracha community of Karnataka, CIIL director Basavaraja Kodagunti explained the unique mathematical expressions preserved in its language, demonstrating the knowledge embedded in indigenous linguistic traditions. As part of the three-day festival, discussions will be held on a National Atlas of Tribal Languages, technology for low-resource languages, and the role of government policies and institutions in strengthening the indigenous language ecosystem. A tribal heritage exhibition organised as part of the festival showcases the everyday cultural life of the Toda, Munda, Soliga, Alu Kurumba, Sora, Gondi and Ulladan communities.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: A live demonstration of Munda Mundua painting by tribal artists was held on Wednesday. Alu Kurumba art will be displayed on Thursday, while Sora painting will be showcased on Friday.

Institutional (Adjective)
संस्थागत — देश की संवैधानिक या सरकारी संस्थाओं के नियमों और ढांचे से जुड़ा हुआ।
✓ Syn: Systemic, Organizational, Constitutional  |  ✖ Ant: Individual, Informal, Unorganized
Indigenous (Adjective)
स्वदेशी — अपने ही देश (भारत) के वैज्ञानिकों और इंजीनियरों द्वारा देश में विकसित किया गया।
✓ Syn: Domestic, Home-grown, Native  |  ✖ Ant: Imported, Foreign, Exotic
Communication (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Communication' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Documentation (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Documentation' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "Language fest showcases culture of tribes", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. A three-day Janjatiya Bhasha Utsava (Tribal Language Festival), organised as part of the Janjatiya Gaurav Divas celebrations honouring tribal freedom...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Language fest showcases culture of tribes' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Language fest showcases culture of tribes' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Language fest showcases culture of tribes' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "A three-day Janjatiya Bhasha Utsava (Tribal Language Festival), organised as part of the Janjatiya Gaurav Divas celebrations honouring tribal freedom..." (Hinglish Arth: आदिवासी स्वतंत्रता सेनानी बिरसा मुंडा के सम्मान में जनजातीय गौरव दिवस समारोह के हिस्से के रूप में आयोजित तीन दिवसीय जनजातीय भाषा उत्सव (आदिवासी भाषा महोत्सव) केंद्रीय भारतीय भाषा संस्थान में चल रहा है।)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Language fest showcases culture of tribes"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. Alu Kurumba art will be displayed on Thursday, while Sora painting will be showcased on Friday.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "Alu Kurumba art will be displayed on Thursday, while Sora painting will be showcased on Friday." (Hinglish Arth: अलु कुरुम्बा कला गुरुवार को प्रदर्शित की जाएगी, जबकि सोरा पेंटिंग शुक्रवार को प्रदर्शित की जाएगी।)

articles.title: Iran strikes U.S. air base in Kuwait, targets Bahrain amid wider Gulf attacks
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Iran said its recent attacks — including those on other U.S. facilities in Bahrain on November 15 and November 13 — were in response to U.S. drone surveillance operations and an attack on Iranian communications towers

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Iran widened its attacks on its Gulf neighbours on Wednesday (November 18, 2026), firing on the U.S. Ali Al Salem air base in Kuwait and Bahrain in what appeared to be retaliation for American strikes the day before. After about two months without such attacks, Iran has repeatedly targeted U.S. facilities in Bahrain in recent days. The small Persian Gulf island kingdom hosts the U.S. Navy’s 5th Fleet. The early morning attacks came after a U.S. fighter jet struck a Revolutionary Guard missile launch site on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz. The U.S. strike was in retaliation for an Iranian strike on an American radar installation in Bahrain earlier on Tuesday (November 17, 2026). Iran said its recent attacks — including those on other U.S. facilities in Bahrain on Sunday (November 15, 2026) and Friday November 13, 2026) — were in response to U.S. drone surveillance operations and an attack on Iranian communications towers. The U.S. military did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the latest attacks. With its economy suffering under a U.S. naval blockade and U.S. military escorts helping restore the passage of oil tankers through the Strait of Hormuz, experts say the recent attacks suggest Tehran may be growing weary of the status quo. “Even if neither side intends to enter a broader confrontation, the accumulation of military incidents across multiple fronts increases the risk of miscalculation and escalation beyond what either side originally intended,” Hamidreza Azizi, senior Iran analyst at the International Crisis Group think tank, wrote in an analysis posted to X following the initial reports of the attack on Kuwait. U.S. President Donald Trump has sent mixed messages on his next steps, saying new strikes are highly unlikely, but also sending a third aircraft carrier and thousands more troops to West Asia. Though U.S. military protection has helped restore oil shipments from the Gulf roughly to prewar levels, Iran has continued to attack tankers as they attempt to transit the Strait of Hormuz.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: United Arab Emirates state-owned oil company ADNOC said on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) that one of its tanker crew members was missing after an attack in the strait the day before, while 11 others were injured and were receiving medical care.

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #19 of 30 (18 NOV)

📰 Iran strikes U.S. air base in Kuwait, targets Bahrain amid wider Gulf attacks

📌 Published: 18 Nov 2026, 07:06:13 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Iran said its recent attacks — including those on other U.S. facilities in Bahrain on November 15 and November 13 — were in response to U.S. drone surveillance operations and an attack on Iranian communications towers

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Iran widened its attacks on its Gulf neighbours on Wednesday (November 18, 2026), firing on the U.S. Ali Al Salem air base in Kuwait and Bahrain in what appeared to be retaliation for American strikes the day before. After about two months without such attacks, Iran has repeatedly targeted U.S. facilities in Bahrain in recent days. The small Persian Gulf island kingdom hosts the U.S. Navy’s 5th Fleet. The early morning attacks came after a U.S. fighter jet struck a Revolutionary Guard missile launch site on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz. The U.S. strike was in retaliation for an Iranian strike on an American radar installation in Bahrain earlier on Tuesday (November 17, 2026). Iran said its recent attacks — including those on other U.S. facilities in Bahrain on Sunday (November 15, 2026) and Friday November 13, 2026) — were in response to U.S. drone surveillance operations and an attack on Iranian communications towers. The U.S. military did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the latest attacks. With its economy suffering under a U.S. naval blockade and U.S. military escorts helping restore the passage of oil tankers through the Strait of Hormuz, experts say the recent attacks suggest Tehran may be growing weary of the status quo. “Even if neither side intends to enter a broader confrontation, the accumulation of military incidents across multiple fronts increases the risk of miscalculation and escalation beyond what either side originally intended,” Hamidreza Azizi, senior Iran analyst at the International Crisis Group think tank, wrote in an analysis posted to X following the initial reports of the attack on Kuwait. U.S. President Donald Trump has sent mixed messages on his next steps, saying new strikes are highly unlikely, but also sending a third aircraft carrier and thousands more troops to West Asia. Though U.S. military protection has helped restore oil shipments from the Gulf roughly to prewar levels, Iran has continued to attack tankers as they attempt to transit the Strait of Hormuz.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: United Arab Emirates state-owned oil company ADNOC said on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) that one of its tanker crew members was missing after an attack in the strait the day before, while 11 others were injured and were receiving medical care.

Miscalculation (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Miscalculation' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।

महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Confrontation' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
International (Adjective)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'International' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Surveillance (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Surveillance' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial

Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🌐 International & Geopolitics passage on "Iran strikes U.S. air base in Kuwait, targets Bahrain amid wider Gulf attacks", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Iran said its recent attacks — including those on other U.S.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Iran strikes U.S. air base in Kuwait, targets Ba' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Iran strikes U.S. air base in Kuwait, targets' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Iran strikes U.S. air base in Kuwait, targets' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Iran said its recent attacks — including those on other U.S." (Hinglish Arth: ईरान ने कहा कि उसके हालिया हमले - जिनमें अन्य अमेरिकी हमले भी शामिल हैं।)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Iran strikes U.S. air base in Kuwait, targets Bahrain amid wider Gulf attacks"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. United Arab Emirates state-owned oil company ADNOC said on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) that one of its tanker crew members was missing after an...
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "United Arab Emirates state-owned oil company ADNOC said on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) that one of its tanker crew members was missing after an..." (Hinglish Arth: संयुक्त अरब अमीरात की सरकारी स्वामित्व वाली तेल कंपनी एडीएनओसी ने बुधवार (18 नवंबर, 2026) को कहा कि उसके टैंकर चालक दल का एक सदस्य एक दिन पहले जलडमरूमध्य में हुए हमले के बाद लापता है, जबकि 11 अन्य घायल हो गए हैं।)

articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The Chinese President opened the two-day APEC gathering with an address to a CEO Summit, where he made a pitch for openness and stable supply chains

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Chinese President Xi Jinping on Wednesday hailed relations with Russia “as a source of stability” in a “turbulent” world, even as he welcomed U.S. President Donald Trump with a rare airport reception a day ahead of a trilateral summit in Shenzhen. On Thursday (November 19, 2026), leaders of the three countries will hold a summit, which Beijing has described as having “groundbreaking significance”. U.S. officials said the three leaders will likely discuss, among other issues, the war in Ukraine, the situation in Iran, global energy stability, and nuclear arms control. 🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #20 of 30 (18 NOV)

📰 Xi hails Russia ties as ‘source of stability’ ahead of trilateral summit

📌 Published: 18 Nov 2026, 07:05:22 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The Chinese President opened the two-day APEC gathering with an address to a CEO Summit, where he made a pitch for openness and stable supply chains

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Chinese President Xi Jinping on Wednesday hailed relations with Russia “as a source of stability” in a “turbulent” world, even as he welcomed U.S. President Donald Trump with a rare airport reception a day ahead of a trilateral summit in Shenzhen. On Thursday (November 19, 2026), leaders of the three countries will hold a summit, which Beijing has described as having “groundbreaking significance”. U.S. officials said the three leaders will likely discuss, among other issues, the war in Ukraine, the situation in Iran, global energy stability, and nuclear arms control. Officials have described the rare trilateral leaders’ summit as more of an exploratory and symbolic meeting, playing down the likelihood of substantive outcomes, either with regard to a possible Russia-Ukraine deal or on the West Asian crisis. Whether they can see eye-to-eye on nuclear disarmament also remains to be seen. At the same time, Beijing has highlighted the symbolism of the summit happening on its soil, describing it as a landmark moment for what China calls “major country diplomacy”. In talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin on Wednesday (November 18, 2026), Mr. Xi described China-Russia relations “as a source of stability and certainty in a turbulent world and as a model of a new type of major-power relationship characterised by equality, mutual respect, trust, and win-win cooperation.” The U.S. President landed in Shenzhen on Wednesday (November 18, 2026), and Mr. Xi welcomed him at the airport with a hug — a rare greeting from the Chinese President, who was reciprocating Mr. Trump similarly receiving him in September at Joint Base Andrews outside Washington. Chinese President Xi Jinping welcomes US President Donald Trump as he arrives at Shenzhen Airport to attend the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Leaders Summit in Shenzhen, China on November 18, 2026. | Photo Credit: Reuters The Chinese President opened the two-day APEC gathering with an address to a CEO Summit, where he made a pitch for openness and stable supply chains. “The world is facing mounting instability, insufficient momentum for economic growth, and a resurgence of unilateralism and protectionism. At the same time, global trade is still growing despite headwinds and emerging technologies are advancing rapidly, reshaping global development,” he said, adding that “the key questions of the age were whether the world would choose openness or closure, cooperation or division, reform or stagnation.”

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Mr. Xi called for barriers to trade and investment to be reduced and proposed establishing a World Bay Area Economic Cooperation Alliance. Beijing has been developing the Greater Bay Area, including Shenzhen, Hong Kong and Macau, as an innovation hub.

Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🌐 International & Geopolitics passage on "Xi hails Russia ties as ‘source of stability’ ahead of trilateral summit", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. The Chinese President opened the two-day APEC gathering with an address to a CEO Summit, where he made a pitch for openness and stable supply chains.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Xi hails Russia ties as ‘source of stability’ ah' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Xi hails Russia ties as ‘source of stability’' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Xi hails Russia ties as ‘source of stability’' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Xi hails Russia ties as ‘source of stability’ ahead of trilateral summit"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. Beijing has been developing the Greater Bay Area, including Shenzhen, Hong Kong and Macau, as an innovation hub.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "Beijing has been developing the Greater Bay Area, including Shenzhen, Hong Kong and Macau, as an innovation hub." (Hinglish Arth: बीजिंग शेन्ज़ेन, हांगकांग और मकाऊ समेत ग्रेटर बे एरिया को इनोवेशन हब के रूप में विकसित कर रहा है।)

articles.title: Scientists warn of growing health threats of chemicals found everywhere
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: EDCs are chemicals that interfere with, mimic, or block the hormones that regulate the development and behaviour of our organs

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Chemicals found almost everywhere in modern life pose a "global and growing threat" to human health and the environment, a landmark report based on over a decade of research has warned. The report on "endocrine-disrupting chemicals" (EDCs) released by the United Nations Environment Programme and World Health Organization "conservatively" estimates the health and environmental costs of EDC exposure at over $1 trillion annually. "The scientific evidence is clear: EDCs are a global and growing threat to human and environmental health," warns the report written by international scientists, calling current regulations "uneven and insufficient." EDCs are chemicals that interfere with, mimic, or block the hormones that regulate the development and behaviour of our organs. They are in everything from toys and makeup, to building materials and clothing. The report released late Tuesday is the first such comprehensive look at EDC impacts in 14 years, and finds increasingly clear links between them and a range of diseases. "The evidence is so strong that it's irrefutable at this point," said Laura Vandenberg, report co-author and professor of environmental health sciences at the University of Massachusetts Amherst. The report examined thousands of studies on chemicals like bisphenols, phthalates and parabens. Evidence of links between these chemicals and disease is strongest for certain neurological conditions and reproductive problems including sperm decline.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: But there is also growing confidence that EDCs are linked to diseases like type 2 diabetes and asthma that have spiked globally.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #30 of 30 (18 NOV)

📰 Scientists warn of growing health threats of chemicals found everywhere

📌 Published: 18 Nov 2026, 08:02:11 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: EDCs are chemicals that interfere with, mimic, or block the hormones that regulate the development and behaviour of our organs

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Chemicals found almost everywhere in modern life pose a "global and growing threat" to human health and the environment, a landmark report based on over a decade of research has warned. The report on "endocrine-disrupting chemicals" (EDCs) released by the United Nations Environment Programme and World Health Organization "conservatively" estimates the health and environmental costs of EDC exposure at over $1 trillion annually. "The scientific evidence is clear: EDCs are a global and growing threat to human and environmental health," warns the report written by international scientists, calling current regulations "uneven and insufficient." EDCs are chemicals that interfere with, mimic, or block the hormones that regulate the development and behaviour of our organs. They are in everything from toys and makeup, to building materials and clothing. The report released late Tuesday is the first such comprehensive look at EDC impacts in 14 years, and finds increasingly clear links between them and a range of diseases. "The evidence is so strong that it's irrefutable at this point," said Laura Vandenberg, report co-author and professor of environmental health sciences at the University of Massachusetts Amherst. The report examined thousands of studies on chemicals like bisphenols, phthalates and parabens. Evidence of links between these chemicals and disease is strongest for certain neurological conditions and reproductive problems including sperm decline.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: But there is also growing confidence that EDCs are linked to diseases like type 2 diabetes and asthma that have spiked globally.

B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Scientists warn of growing health threats of che' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Scientists warn of growing health threats of ' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Scientists warn of growing health threats of ' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Scientists warn of growing health threats of chemicals found everywhere"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. But there is also growing confidence that EDCs are linked to diseases like type 2 diabetes and asthma that have spiked globally.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "But there is also growing confidence that EDCs are linked to diseases like type 2 diabetes and asthma that have spiked globally." (Hinglish Arth: लेकिन यह विश्वास भी बढ़ रहा है कि ईडीसी टाइप 2 मधुमेह और अस्थमा जैसी बीमारियों से जुड़े हैं जो विश्व स्तर पर तेजी से बढ़ी हैं।)

articles.title: Researchers boost gut microbial activity linked to longevity in aged mice, find improved metabolism
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The study suggests that specific age-related changes in the gut microbiome may be protective adaptations rather than signs of decline, and could potentially be harnessed to support healthier ageing

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Researchers have identified changes in the metabolic activity of the gut microbiome associated with exceptional longevity in humans, and found that amplifying the same activity in aged mice using engineered bacteria improved metabolic health. Published in the journal Cell Metabolism , the team's study suggests that specific age-related changes in the gut microbiome may be protective adaptations rather than signs of decline, and could potentially be harnessed to support healthier aging. Senior author Amir Zarrinpar, chair in circadian biology and medicine, and professor of medicine at the University of California San Diego, said while many studies on aging focus on what goes wrong as one grows old, the findings suggest "some changes in the gut microbiome may actually represent the body's attempt to preserve metabolic health". "If we can identify those beneficial functions and safely strengthen them, we may eventually be able to develop new ways to promote healthier aging," Zarrinpar said. The gut microbiome, the community of bacteria and other microbes living in the digestive tract, is known to change throughout life and plays an important role in metabolism and inflammation, among other aspects of health. Studies have also found distinctive microbiome features among people who age exceptionally well. The researchers focused on how gut microbes modify bile acids, substances produced by the liver that help digest fats but also act as signalling molecules in the body. Studying young and aged mice, they found that aging was associated with an increased microbial activity linked to enzymes called bile salt hydrolases. These enzymes chemically modify bile acids, allowing them to influence pathways involved in metabolism, inflammation and the body's internal clock. The team also found greater bile acid modification in the mice.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: To determine patterns in humans, they reanalysed publicly available data from a human ageing cohort, analysing bile acid measurements from 48 young adults, 107 older adults and 125 centenarians.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #30 of 30 (18 NOV)

📰 Researchers boost gut microbial activity linked to longevity in aged mice, find improved metabolism

📌 Published: 18 Nov 2026, 07:53:42 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The study suggests that specific age-related changes in the gut microbiome may be protective adaptations rather than signs of decline, and could potentially be harnessed to support healthier ageing

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Researchers have identified changes in the metabolic activity of the gut microbiome associated with exceptional longevity in humans, and found that amplifying the same activity in aged mice using engineered bacteria improved metabolic health. Published in the journal Cell Metabolism , the team's study suggests that specific age-related changes in the gut microbiome may be protective adaptations rather than signs of decline, and could potentially be harnessed to support healthier aging. Senior author Amir Zarrinpar, chair in circadian biology and medicine, and professor of medicine at the University of California San Diego, said while many studies on aging focus on what goes wrong as one grows old, the findings suggest "some changes in the gut microbiome may actually represent the body's attempt to preserve metabolic health". "If we can identify those beneficial functions and safely strengthen them, we may eventually be able to develop new ways to promote healthier aging," Zarrinpar said. The gut microbiome, the community of bacteria and other microbes living in the digestive tract, is known to change throughout life and plays an important role in metabolism and inflammation, among other aspects of health. Studies have also found distinctive microbiome features among people who age exceptionally well. The researchers focused on how gut microbes modify bile acids, substances produced by the liver that help digest fats but also act as signalling molecules in the body. Studying young and aged mice, they found that aging was associated with an increased microbial activity linked to enzymes called bile salt hydrolases. These enzymes chemically modify bile acids, allowing them to influence pathways involved in metabolism, inflammation and the body's internal clock. The team also found greater bile acid modification in the mice.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: To determine patterns in humans, they reanalysed publicly available data from a human ageing cohort, analysing bile acid measurements from 48 young adults, 107 older adults and 125 centenarians.

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Indian laws protect the decision not to have a child through statutes, schemes and subsidies, but the decision to have one is left to the mercy of the private assisted reproduction healthcare market

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The reproductive-autonomy jurisprudence as evolved by the Supreme Court under Article 21 of the Constitution is rich yet narrow, focusing primarily on one side of the problem. In Suchita Srivastava v. Chandigarh Administration (2009), the Court held that reproductive choices may be exercised to procreate as well as to abstain from procreating. In X v. Principal Secretary, Health and Family Welfare Department (2022), the Supreme Court extended the right to abortion to unmarried women as an exercise of ‘decisional autonomy’.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: These, and nearly all other landmark cases are concerned only with an existing pregnancy. The freedom to pursue parenthood through medical treatment, however, has surfaced only at the margins. The Delhi High Court, in 2023, allowed parole of a life convict to attempt IVF, by recognising a “right to parenthood,” but only as a claim against a barrier the State itself had erected. No court has yet asked whether the State may leave a citizen’s access to infertility care entirely to their own purse. Can a right available to the fertile but structurally withheld from the infertile be called a universal right?

In Suchita Srivastava v. Chandigarh Administration (2009), the Court held that reproductive choices may be exercised to procreate as well as to abstain from procreating. In X v. Principal Secretary, Health and Family Welfare Department (2022), the Supreme Court extended the right to abortion to unmarried women as an exercise of ‘decisional autonomy’.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: These, and nearly all other landmark cases are concerned only with an existing pregnancy. The freedom to pursue parenthood through medical treatment, however, has surfaced only at the margins. The Delhi High Court, in 2023, allowed parole of a life convict to attempt IVF, by recognising a “right to parenthood,” but only as a claim against a barrier the State itself had erected. No court has yet asked whether the State may leave a citizen’s access to infertility care entirely to their own purse. Can a right available to the fertile but structurally withheld from the infertile be called a universal right?

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: These, and nearly all other landmark cases are concerned only with an existing pregnancy. The Delhi High Court, in 2023, allowed parole of a life convict to attempt IVF, by recognising a “right to parenthood,” but only as a claim against a barrier the State itself had erected. No court has yet asked whether the State may leave a citizen’s access to infertility care entirely to their own purse. Can a right available to the fertile but structurally withheld from the infertile be called a universal right?

articles.title: Cyclone Akvan: why is Andhra Pradesh facing a third cyclone in a month?
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Warm seas, river water that traps heat near the surface and winds that steer storms towards the coast have made this post-monsoon season unusual, experts say

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Andhra Pradesh is currently facing a rare weather phenomenon. Since October 28, the State has already been hit by two back-to-back cyclonic storms, and there is an imminent threat of another one battering the coastal districts in the next two days. On October 28, the State was battered by very severe cyclonic storm Arnab , which made landfall near Narsapur in West Godavari district. On November 3, it was hit again by severe cyclonic storm Murasu , which made landfall close to Ongole in Prakasam district. Now, cyclonic storm Akvan is likely to intensify into a very severe cyclonic storm and make landfall on November 20 between Narsapur and Puri. Three tropical storms battering the coast within less than a month during the post-monsoon season is a rare scenario. The last times such a thing happened were in 1976, 1987 and 2013. Both 1976 and 1987 were El Niño years, and this year is also categorised as a super El Niño year . When it comes to tropical cyclones over the Bay of Bengal, there are a number of driving factors, and El Niño is just one of them. Mostly, the formation of storms over the Bay, especially their frequency and intensity, differs slightly from the rest of the world, because the Bay of Bengal is almost a land-locked sea, said S.S.V.S. Ramakrishna, former head of the Department of Oceanography and Meteorology, Andhra University, who has spent over four decades researching the pattern of cyclones over the Bay. “El Niño typically suppresses the southwest summer monsoon over India, but it has the opposite effect on the Northeast (winter) Monsoon and post-monsoon cyclogenesis in the Bay of Bengal,” he said. El Niño drought then floods hit North Andhra farmers El Niño, a deficient monsoon, and the heat to come During El Niño years, the northeast monsoon tends to be significantly more active over southern peninsular India. This creates continuous moisture convergence and frequent convective disturbances over the southern Bay, providing a steady assembly line of low-pressure areas. And sometimes, in rare occurrences, remnants of a Pacific Ocean cyclone cross the Strait of Malacca, re-enter the Bay of Bengal, and intensify into a cyclone. “We had seen this phenomenon during the Odisha Super Cyclone in 1999,” he said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Mr. Ramakrishna also pointed out that in October and November, the Bay of Bengal consistently retained high sea surface temperatures—over 26.5 degrees Celsius—and anything above 26 is conducive to developing a cyclonic system. This has been aided by the El Niño-modified upper-level wind patterns over the southern Bay of Bengal, which reduce vertical wind shear.

• 1. Core Context & Background: Warm seas, river water that traps heat near the surface and winds that steer storms towards the coast have made this post-monsoon season unusual, experts say
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Andhra Pradesh is currently facing a rare weather phenomenon. Since October 28, the State has already been hit by two back-to-back cyclonic storms, and there is an imminent threat of another one battering the coastal districts in the next two days. On October 28, the State was battered by very severe cyclonic storm Arnab , which made landfall near Narsapur in West Godavari district. On November 3, it was hit again by severe cyclonic storm Murasu , which made landfall close to Ongole in Prakasam district. Now, cyclonic storm Akvan is likely to intensify into a very severe cyclonic storm and make landfall on November 20 between Narsapur and Puri. Three tropical storms battering the coast within less than a month during the post-monsoon season is a rare scenario. The last times such a thing happened were in 1976, 1987 and 2013. Both 1976 and 1987 were El Niño years, and this year is also categorised as a super El Niño year . When it comes to tropical cyclones over the Bay of Bengal, there are a number of driving factors, and El Niño is just one of them. Mostly, the formation of storms over the Bay, especially their frequency and intensity, differs slightly from the rest of the world, because the Bay of Bengal is almost a land-locked sea, said S.S.V.S. Ramakrishna, former head of the Department of Oceanography and Meteorology, Andhra University, who has spent over four decades researching the pattern of cyclones over the Bay. “El Niño typically suppresses the southwest summer monsoon over India, but it has the opposite effect on the Northeast (winter) Monsoon and post-monsoon cyclogenesis in the Bay of Bengal,” he said. El Niño drought then floods hit North Andhra farmers El Niño, a deficient monsoon, and the heat to come During El Niño years, the northeast monsoon tends to be significantly more active over southern peninsular India. This creates continuous moisture convergence and frequent convective disturbances over the southern Bay, providing a steady assembly line of low-pressure areas. And sometimes, in rare occurrences, remnants of a Pacific Ocean cyclone cross the Strait of Malacca, re-enter the Bay of Bengal, and intensify into a cyclone. “We had seen this phenomenon during the Odisha Super Cyclone in 1999,” he said.
• 3. This has been aided by the El Niño-modified upper-level wind patterns over the southern Bay of Bengal, which reduce vertical wind shear.

articles.title: Air purifier sales surge as demand, smart features drive market growth
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: While Delhi-NCR remains the dominant market, cities like Mumbai and regions beyond traditional high-pollution belts are showing sustained upticks

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Demand for air purifiers in India has witnessed explosive growth in 2026, with major brands and retail platforms reporting sales doubling or tripling year-on-year. Driven by an early surge ahead of the traditional winter pollution season , consumer behaviour is shifting toward viewing indoor air quality as a year-round health priority rather than an emergency seasonal purchase. According to industry leaders, adoption is gaining momentum well before peak pollution months. Smart tech brand Qubo recorded a 150 percent growth over the previous year, while Xiaomi registered approximately 3X year-on-year sales growth during the festive period. Industry executives note that growing awareness surrounding indoor pollutants, ranging from dust and pet dander to everyday cooking and cleaning emissions, is encouraging households to take a proactive approach to home wellness throughout the year. Retail footprint and online traffic reflect this expanding market footprint across the country. Electronics retailer Croma reported that air purifier sales volumes have more than doubled in 2026. While Delhi-NCR remains the dominant market, cities like Mumbai and regions beyond traditional high-pollution belts are showing sustained upticks. Premium tech maker Dyson also reported that visits to its air purifier pages grew by over 100 percent in October compared to the same period last year. Modern buyers are increasingly seeking advanced functionality and intelligent filtration tech. Croma highlighted strong consumer interest in models featuring real-time AQI displays, app controls, and multi-functional units combining purification with humidification or heating. On e-commerce platforms, Amazon India reported that sales doubled over the past week. Shoppers are actively leveraging Rufus, Amazon’s personalised AI shopping assistant, to filter models by room size, filter type, and live sensor capabilities, prompting the e-retailer to expand selection on Amazon Now for immediate delivery. “We have observed a notable increase in consumer demand for air purifiers on Flipkart, reflected in higher search activity, product discovery and purchases. Northern India continues to account for a significant share of demand for the category. We also witnessed a rise in purchases during the early hours following Diwali, coinciding with heightened concerns around deteriorating air quality and the steps households are taking to manage their indoor environments,” said Flipkart.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: technology (general) / gadgets (general) / accessories
