🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #30 of 30 (18 NOV)

📰 Air purifier sales surge as demand, smart features drive market growth

📌 Published: 18 Nov 2026, 05:23:18 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: While Delhi-NCR remains the dominant market, cities like Mumbai and regions beyond traditional high-pollution belts are showing sustained upticks

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Demand for air purifiers in India has witnessed explosive growth in 2026, with major brands and retail platforms reporting sales doubling or tripling year-on-year. Driven by an early surge ahead of the traditional winter pollution season , consumer behaviour is shifting toward viewing indoor air quality as a year-round health priority rather than an emergency seasonal purchase. According to industry leaders, adoption is gaining momentum well before peak pollution months. Smart tech brand Qubo recorded a 150 percent growth over the previous year, while Xiaomi registered approximately 3X year-on-year sales growth during the festive period. Industry executives note that growing awareness surrounding indoor pollutants, ranging from dust and pet dander to everyday cooking and cleaning emissions, is encouraging households to take a proactive approach to home wellness throughout the year. Retail footprint and online traffic reflect this expanding market footprint across the country. Electronics retailer Croma reported that air purifier sales volumes have more than doubled in 2026. While Delhi-NCR remains the dominant market, cities like Mumbai and regions beyond traditional high-pollution belts are showing sustained upticks. Premium tech maker Dyson also reported that visits to its air purifier pages grew by over 100 percent in October compared to the same period last year. Modern buyers are increasingly seeking advanced functionality and intelligent filtration tech. Croma highlighted strong consumer interest in models featuring real-time AQI displays, app controls, and multi-functional units combining purification with humidification or heating. On e-commerce platforms, Amazon India reported that sales doubled over the past week. Shoppers are actively leveraging Rufus, Amazon’s personalised AI shopping assistant, to filter models by room size, filter type, and live sensor capabilities, prompting the e-retailer to expand selection on Amazon Now for immediate delivery. “We have observed a notable increase in consumer demand for air purifiers on Flipkart, reflected in higher search activity, product discovery and purchases. Northern India continues to account for a significant share of demand for the category. We also witnessed a rise in purchases during the early hours following Diwali, coinciding with heightened concerns around deteriorating air quality and the steps households are taking to manage their indoor environments,” said Flipkart.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: technology (general) / gadgets (general) / accessories

जवाबदेही — अपने फैसलों और काम का जनता तथा संविधान को हिसाब देने की बाध्यता।
✓ Syn: Responsibility, Answerability, Liability  |  ✖ Ant: Immunity, Exemption, Irresponsibility
Sustainability (Noun)
सतत विकास — पर्यावरण और भविष्य की पीढ़ियों को नुकसान पहुँचाए बिना लंबे समय तक चलने वाला विकास।
✓ Syn: Viability, Eco-balance, Durability  |  ✖ Ant: Depletion, Unsustainability, Destruction
Humidification (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Humidification' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial

A. While Delhi-NCR remains the dominant market, cities like Mumbai and regions beyond traditional high-pollution belts are showing sustained upticks.

D. The author contends that 'Air purifier sales surge as demand, smart fea' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Air purifier sales surge as demand, smart features drive market growth"?

articles.title: Purandeshwari calls for political consensus on women’s reservation
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Political parties should arrive at a consensus on providing 33% reservation to women in Parliament and all State legislatures, said D. Purandeshwari, chairperson of the Commonwealth Women Parliamentarians (CWP) India Region, here on Wednesday.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: “Political parties should explore the possibility of providing reservation to women by delinking it from the Census exercise and advancing the delimitation process. This can be based on the 2011 Census. The legislation has been linked to the Census and delimitation, which could defer its implementation until 2030 if the Census exercise takes place in 2027,” she told presspersons after the two-day meeting of the CWP India Region concluded here on Wednesday. “On a significant issue such as women’s reservation, political parties should come together, overcoming all political differences.” The two-day event concluded on Wednesday with the adoption of resolutions focusing on strengthening women’s leadership, addressing technology-driven challenges, and destigmatising menopause. Asked whether women parliamentarians were being given adequate time to participate in debates and whether they were being consulted during the legislative process, she said Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla had taken a conscious decision to provide every woman parliamentarian an opportunity to speak in each session.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Ms. Purandeshwari said there is a need to offer training to women representatives in policy, financial management and legislative matters, and that the possibility of zonal training programmes was being explored. “This was the first meeting of women parliamentarians from across India. The recommendations collated from the sessions would be escalated to the government level where policy intervention is required, while others would be taken up directly by women representatives for women’s empowerment,” she said.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #7 of 30 (18 NOV)

📰 Purandeshwari calls for political consensus on women’s reservation

📌 Published: 18 Nov 2026, 09:25:46 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Political parties should arrive at a consensus on providing 33% reservation to women in Parliament and all State legislatures, said D. Purandeshwari, chairperson of the Commonwealth Women Parliamentarians (CWP) India Region, here on Wednesday.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: “Political parties should explore the possibility of providing reservation to women by delinking it from the Census exercise and advancing the delimitation process. This can be based on the 2011 Census. The legislation has been linked to the Census and delimitation, which could defer its implementation until 2030 if the Census exercise takes place in 2027,” she told presspersons after the two-day meeting of the CWP India Region concluded here on Wednesday. “On a significant issue such as women’s reservation, political parties should come together, overcoming all political differences.” The two-day event concluded on Wednesday with the adoption of resolutions focusing on strengthening women’s leadership, addressing technology-driven challenges, and destigmatising menopause. Asked whether women parliamentarians were being given adequate time to participate in debates and whether they were being consulted during the legislative process, she said Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla had taken a conscious decision to provide every woman parliamentarian an opportunity to speak in each session.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Ms. Purandeshwari said there is a need to offer training to women representatives in policy, financial management and legislative matters, and that the possibility of zonal training programmes was being explored. “This was the first meeting of women parliamentarians from across India. The recommendations collated from the sessions would be escalated to the government level where policy intervention is required, while others would be taken up directly by women representatives for women’s empowerment,” she said.

क्रियान्वयन / ज़मीनी स्तर पर लागू करना — किसी योजना या फैसले को असलियत में पूरा करना।
✓ Syn: Execution, Enforcement, Fulfillment  |  ✖ Ant: Abandonment, Neglect, Cancellation

महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Delimitation' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Restrictive, Counteractive, Adverse  |  ✖ Ant: Constructive, Supportive, Favorable
Intervention (Adjective / Verb)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Intervention' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Restrictive, Counteractive, Adverse  |  ✖ Ant: Constructive, Supportive, Favorable
Reservation (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Reservation' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial

Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "Purandeshwari calls for political consensus on women’s reservation", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Political parties should arrive at a consensus on providing 33% reservation to women in Parliament and all State legislatures, said D.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Purandeshwari calls for political consensus on w' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Purandeshwari calls for political consensus o' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Purandeshwari calls for political consensus o' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Political parties should arrive at a consensus on providing 33% reservation to women in Parliament and all State legislatures, said D." Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Purandeshwari calls for political consensus on women’s reservation"?

C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.

articles.title: Video showing Tamil Nadu Minister getting close to wild elephant will be probed: Karnataka Forest Minister
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Forest and Environment Minister Ramalinga Reddy has instructed officials to investigate a video which allegedly shows Tamil Nadu Minister for Social Justice, Adi Dravidar Welfare and Hill Tribes Vanni Arasu getting close to a wild elephant while travelling in a vehicle belonging to the Karnataka Forest Department.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The incident is said to have occurred in the Bandipur Tiger Reserve, and the video of it has been circulating on social media. “The video link was also shared with me. I have seen it. The registration number of the vehicle is also visible,” Mr. Reddy said on Wednesday, He added that he has instructed officials to probe the matter and that a thorough investigation would be conducted. “I will write to our Principal Chief Conservator of Forests (PCCF) as well as the Director General of Police and Inspector General of Police about this issue. The matter will be thoroughly investigated. No matter what their position is, everyone must follow the rules and regulations applicable in forest areas,” Mr. Reddy said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Mr. Vanni Arasu has also been facing criticism for allegedly pursuing a tiger inside the Mudumalai Tiger Reserve. A video circulating on social media allegedly shows him running after a tiger. The same video allegedly shows Mr. Vanni Arasu getting close to the wild elephant in the Bandipur Tiger Reserve.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #8 of 30 (18 NOV)

📰 Video showing Tamil Nadu Minister getting close to wild elephant will be probed: Karnataka Forest Minister

📌 Published: 18 Nov 2026, 09:25:25 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Forest and Environment Minister Ramalinga Reddy has instructed officials to investigate a video which allegedly shows Tamil Nadu Minister for Social Justice, Adi Dravidar Welfare and Hill Tribes Vanni Arasu getting close to a wild elephant while travelling in a vehicle belonging to the Karnataka Forest Department.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The incident is said to have occurred in the Bandipur Tiger Reserve, and the video of it has been circulating on social media. “The video link was also shared with me. I have seen it. The registration number of the vehicle is also visible,” Mr. Reddy said on Wednesday, He added that he has instructed officials to probe the matter and that a thorough investigation would be conducted. “I will write to our Principal Chief Conservator of Forests (PCCF) as well as the Director General of Police and Inspector General of Police about this issue. The matter will be thoroughly investigated. No matter what their position is, everyone must follow the rules and regulations applicable in forest areas,” Mr. Reddy said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Mr. Vanni Arasu has also been facing criticism for allegedly pursuing a tiger inside the Mudumalai Tiger Reserve. A video circulating on social media allegedly shows him running after a tiger. The same video allegedly shows Mr. Vanni Arasu getting close to the wild elephant in the Bandipur Tiger Reserve.

articles.title: National sociology conference to focus on urban slums, inclusion
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The 18th meeting will be held at the Suvarna Mahotsava Hall of Karnatak University in Dharwad on Friday and Saturday

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The 18th National Sociology Conference, focusing on slums in urban India, social inclusion and justice, will be held at the Suvarna Mahotsava Hall of Karnatak University in Dharwad on Friday and Saturday. The conference, on the theme, Slums in Urban India, Social Inclusion and Justice: Locating the Urban Marginalised Communities, is being organised by the Karnataka Sociological Association and the Department of Sociology, Karnatak University, in association with the Karnataka Slum Development Board and Hubballi-Dharwad Municipal Corporation, under the PM-USHA scheme, according to a release from Head of the Department of Sociology, Karnatak University, Subhashchandra C. Natikar, who is also Organising Secretary of the national conference. Labour and Employment Minister and district in-charge Santosh S. Lad will inaugurate the conference at 10 a.m. on Friday. Union Minister Pralhad Joshi and Legislative Council Chairman Saleem Ahmed will be present. Karnataka Slum Development Board chairman Prasad Abbayya will release the conference proceedings. Professor of Sociology at Jamia Millia Islamia University, New Delhi, Aravinder A. Ansari, who is also secretary of the Indian Sociological Society, will deliver the keynote address. Karnatak University Vice-Chancellor A.M. Khan will release a souvenir. More than 500 sociologists, researchers, faculty members and research scholars from across the country are expected to participate. Around 300 abstracts and 226 research papers will be presented, said Prof. Natikar.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The conference will feature sessions on urban inequality, social exclusion and injustice, religion and politics and rural-urban continuity.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #9 of 30 (18 NOV)

📰 National sociology conference to focus on urban slums, inclusion

📌 Published: 18 Nov 2026, 09:25:18 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The 18th meeting will be held at the Suvarna Mahotsava Hall of Karnatak University in Dharwad on Friday and Saturday

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The 18th National Sociology Conference, focusing on slums in urban India, social inclusion and justice, will be held at the Suvarna Mahotsava Hall of Karnatak University in Dharwad on Friday and Saturday. The conference, on the theme, Slums in Urban India, Social Inclusion and Justice: Locating the Urban Marginalised Communities, is being organised by the Karnataka Sociological Association and the Department of Sociology, Karnatak University, in association with the Karnataka Slum Development Board and Hubballi-Dharwad Municipal Corporation, under the PM-USHA scheme, according to a release from Head of the Department of Sociology, Karnatak University, Subhashchandra C. Natikar, who is also Organising Secretary of the national conference. Labour and Employment Minister and district in-charge Santosh S. Lad will inaugurate the conference at 10 a.m. on Friday. Union Minister Pralhad Joshi and Legislative Council Chairman Saleem Ahmed will be present. Karnataka Slum Development Board chairman Prasad Abbayya will release the conference proceedings. Professor of Sociology at Jamia Millia Islamia University, New Delhi, Aravinder A. Ansari, who is also secretary of the Indian Sociological Society, will deliver the keynote address. Karnatak University Vice-Chancellor A.M. Khan will release a souvenir. More than 500 sociologists, researchers, faculty members and research scholars from across the country are expected to participate. Around 300 abstracts and 226 research papers will be presented, said Prof. Natikar.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The conference will feature sessions on urban inequality, social exclusion and injustice, religion and politics and rural-urban continuity.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu’s latest representation on Mekedatu has no reference to the tribunal demand
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: No communication is said to have been issued by the Union government to Karnataka for comments, sources in the State government say

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Tamil Nadu’s latest representation to the Union government on the controversial Mekedatu dam project has no reference to the demand for a new tribunal to go into the project. However, the present move to meet Union Minister for Jal Shakti C.R. Patil was in response to Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar’s recent observations on the Mekedatu project. On November 14, Mr Shivakkumar asserted Karnataka would go ahead with the Mekedatu project, describing it as the State’s right and duty, while assuring that Tamil Nadu would receive its stipulated share of Cauvery water. The previous Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) regime, at the fag end of its term, had sent the complaint to the Centre. But, this was kept under wraps till Leader of Opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin, who was Deputy Chief Minister till May, referred to it during the debate in the Assembly in June on the Mekedatu issue, after which a resolution was adopted on the issue. Describing the project as “inadmissible” and “impermissible,” the State government, in the communication, had contended that the project “is beyond the scope of the 2007 final award of the Cauvery Water Disputes Tribunal (CWDT) and the Supreme Court’s judgment of 2018.”
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam / Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam / Cauvery Mahapushkaram 2017 / water / water rights / Karnataka / Tamil Nadu

📰 Tamil Nadu’s latest representation on Mekedatu has no reference to the tribunal demand

Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Tamil Nadu’s latest representation to the Union government on the controversial Mekedatu dam project has no reference to the demand for a new tribunal to go into the project. However, the present move to meet Union Minister for Jal Shakti C.R. Patil was in response to Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar’s recent observations on the Mekedatu project. On November 14, Mr Shivakkumar asserted Karnataka would go ahead with the Mekedatu project, describing it as the State’s right and duty, while assuring that Tamil Nadu would receive its stipulated share of Cauvery water. The previous Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) regime, at the fag end of its term, had sent the complaint to the Centre. But, this was kept under wraps till Leader of Opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin, who was Deputy Chief Minister till May, referred to it during the debate in the Assembly in June on the Mekedatu issue, after which a resolution was adopted on the issue. Describing the project as “inadmissible” and “impermissible,” the State government, in the communication, had contended that the project “is beyond the scope of the 2007 final award of the Cauvery Water Disputes Tribunal (CWDT) and the Supreme Court’s judgment of 2018.”

articles.title: State awards work orders to eight start-ups under ‘Government First Initiative’
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The first batch of eight startups to develop tech solutoins for Praja Seva Department and the Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board (BWSSB)

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The State government on Wednesday awarded direct work orders to eight start-ups under its “Government First Initiative” to build technology solutions for the Praja Seva Department and the Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board (BWSSB). The initiative, announced on the second day of the 29th edition of Bengaluru Tech Summit (BTS) 2026 at the Bangalore International Exhibition Centre (BIEC), is expected to connect innovators directly with State departments to solve public sector challenges. Under the programme, each winning start-up is eligible for a direct work order of up to ₹25 lakh. The total committed project value stands at ₹99.78 lakh (inclusive of GST) for the Praja Seva Department, while it is ₹1 crore for the BWSSB. According to the government, the winners emerged from a competitive pool of 150 applications submitted between October 8 and October 23, 2026, with the Praja Seva receiving 76 entries and the BWSSB receiving 74. The rigorous five-stage selection process included application submission, eligibility screening, selection committee evaluation, discussions with respective department officials, and final budget negotiations. The committee assessed start-ups on innovation, technical soundness, product readiness, scalability, and integration capability. Four start-ups were selected to modernise citizen services and administrative workflows for the Praja Seva Department and each was awarded ₹25 lakh. These include: SanMejora, to develop an AI-enabled grievance management and redressal system; VTT AI Private Limited, to create an unified citizen call centre; Datafrontier Innovations Private Limited, to build an AI-enabled e-Office and unified officer workflow platform and Nife Apps Labs, to ensure the uptime and availability of citizen-facing government IT services. Another set of four start-ups were chosen across five challenge areas to optimise urban water infrastructure for the BWSSB and these include: Smart Terra, for an AI and digital innovation challenge focused on urban water management and reducing non-revenue water; UniaX Technologies, to deploy an intelligent asset management solution; Krishi Hrudya Private Limited, to implement GIS-enabled revenue and operational intelligence and Calypsion Innovations LLP, to develop a digital twin for integrated water management. Highlighting the vision behind the programme, Priyank Kharge, Minister for Home and Information Technology & Biotechnology and E-Governance, said, “The initiative reflects our commitment to making government an active partner and customer of Karnataka’s start-up ecosystem. Under the programme, each winning start-up is eligible for a direct work order of up to ₹25 lakh. The total committed project value stands at ₹99.78 lakh (inclusive of GST) for the Praja Seva Department, while it is ₹1 crore for the BWSSB. 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The Government First Initiative is a pioneering policy by the State government that makes the State the first customer for local start-ups developing technology-driven solutions to public sector and governance challenges.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #11 of 30 (18 NOV)

📰 State awards work orders to eight start-ups under ‘Government First Initiative’

📌 Published: 18 Nov 2026, 09:24:15 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The first batch of eight startups to develop tech solutoins for Praja Seva Department and the Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board (BWSSB)

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The State government on Wednesday awarded direct work orders to eight start-ups under its “Government First Initiative” to build technology solutions for the Praja Seva Department and the Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board (BWSSB). The initiative, announced on the second day of the 29th edition of Bengaluru Tech Summit (BTS) 2026 at the Bangalore International Exhibition Centre (BIEC), is expected to connect innovators directly with State departments to solve public sector challenges. Under the programme, each winning start-up is eligible for a direct work order of up to ₹25 lakh. The total committed project value stands at ₹99.78 lakh (inclusive of GST) for the Praja Seva Department, while it is ₹1 crore for the BWSSB. According to the government, the winners emerged from a competitive pool of 150 applications submitted between October 8 and October 23, 2026, with the Praja Seva receiving 76 entries and the BWSSB receiving 74. The rigorous five-stage selection process included application submission, eligibility screening, selection committee evaluation, discussions with respective department officials, and final budget negotiations. The committee assessed start-ups on innovation, technical soundness, product readiness, scalability, and integration capability. Four start-ups were selected to modernise citizen services and administrative workflows for the Praja Seva Department and each was awarded ₹25 lakh. These include: SanMejora, to develop an AI-enabled grievance management and redressal system; VTT AI Private Limited, to create an unified citizen call centre; Datafrontier Innovations Private Limited, to build an AI-enabled e-Office and unified officer workflow platform and Nife Apps Labs, to ensure the uptime and availability of citizen-facing government IT services. Another set of four start-ups were chosen across five challenge areas to optimise urban water infrastructure for the BWSSB and these include: Smart Terra, for an AI and digital innovation challenge focused on urban water management and reducing non-revenue water; UniaX Technologies, to deploy an intelligent asset management solution; Krishi Hrudya Private Limited, to implement GIS-enabled revenue and operational intelligence and Calypsion Innovations LLP, to develop a digital twin for integrated water management. Highlighting the vision behind the programme, Priyank Kharge, Minister for Home and Information Technology & Biotechnology and E-Governance, said, “The initiative reflects our commitment to making government an active partner and customer of Karnataka’s start-up ecosystem. We want to create opportunities for start-ups to take their innovations beyond the proof-of-concept stage and demonstrate their solutions in real-world governance settings.” Responding to media queries, the Minister said other government departments might also come up with respective problem statements, allowing a large number of start-ups to develop solutions and work with the government.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The Government First Initiative is a pioneering policy by the State government that makes the State the first customer for local start-ups developing technology-driven solutions to public sector and governance challenges.

महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Administrative' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।

articles.title: Pan-Indian study finds that higher levels of DNA fragments in blood strengthen cancer signals
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: CancerSpot test records 72% detection rate and 1.4% false positives; the test aims to detect multiple types of cancer through a single blood test, without requiring a tissue biopsy for the initial detection

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A blood test that looks for cancer-related changes in DNA has shown the potential to detect multiple types of cancer. In a study, the test detected 72% of cancer cases, with a false-positive rate of 1.4%. The blood test, CancerSpot, developed by Bengaluru-based Strand Life Sciences, uses DNA sequencing and Artificial Intelligence (AI) to identify changes in DNA that can indicate the presence of cancer. The research, involving 1,480 participants and 43 hospitals across India, including five in Karnataka, was conducted over four years as part of the development and clinical validation of the test. The findings have been published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences (PNAS) , a peer-reviewed scientific journal. Cells in the body release small fragments of DNA into the bloodstream. These are known as circulating or cell-free DNA. In people with cancer, some of these fragments originate from tumour cells and carry changes that can help identify the disease. CancerSpot combines DNA sequencing with AI-based analysis to examine patterns of DNA methylation. Methylation refers to chemical modifications of DNA that influence how genes function. These patterns differ between cancer cells and normal cells and can be used to identify cancer-associated signals in a blood sample. By analysing these patterns, the test aims to detect multiple types of cancer through a single blood test, without requiring a tissue biopsy for the initial detection, said Ramesh Hariharan, CEO of Strand Life Sciences, who is one of the authors of the study. The study examined how DNA released by different cells in the body influences the detection of cancer. An important finding was that higher levels of circulating DNA were associated with stronger cancer-related signals and better detection sensitivity, even among patients at the same stage of cancer. Researchers had expected that the increased release of DNA from immune cells in cancer patients would dilute the tumour-derived DNA signals, making cancer detection more difficult. However, the study found the opposite. The findings suggest that DNA released by tumour cells and immune cells increases together in cancer patients, helping strengthen the cancer-related signals in the blood. This provides new insights into the interaction between tumours and the immune system and its role in blood-based cancer detection, explained Mr. Hariharan, who is also an Adjunct Professor at the Indian Institute of Science, Bengaluru. CancerSpot was evaluated in newly diagnosed patients with 14 types of cancer and healthy individuals. In an independent validation cohort, it detected 72% of patients with cancer, with a false-positive rate of 1.4%.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: A low false-positive rate is important in cancer screening, as it can help reduce unnecessary follow-up investigations and invasive procedures among healthy individuals.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #12 of 30 (18 NOV)

📰 Pan-Indian study finds that higher levels of DNA fragments in blood strengthen cancer signals

📌 Published: 18 Nov 2026, 09:23:02 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: CancerSpot test records 72% detection rate and 1.4% false positives; the test aims to detect multiple types of cancer through a single blood test, without requiring a tissue biopsy for the initial detection

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A blood test that looks for cancer-related changes in DNA has shown the potential to detect multiple types of cancer. In a study, the test detected 72% of cancer cases, with a false-positive rate of 1.4%. The blood test, CancerSpot, developed by Bengaluru-based Strand Life Sciences, uses DNA sequencing and Artificial Intelligence (AI) to identify changes in DNA that can indicate the presence of cancer. The research, involving 1,480 participants and 43 hospitals across India, including five in Karnataka, was conducted over four years as part of the development and clinical validation of the test. The findings have been published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences (PNAS) , a peer-reviewed scientific journal. Cells in the body release small fragments of DNA into the bloodstream. These are known as circulating or cell-free DNA. In people with cancer, some of these fragments originate from tumour cells and carry changes that can help identify the disease. CancerSpot combines DNA sequencing with AI-based analysis to examine patterns of DNA methylation. Methylation refers to chemical modifications of DNA that influence how genes function. These patterns differ between cancer cells and normal cells and can be used to identify cancer-associated signals in a blood sample. By analysing these patterns, the test aims to detect multiple types of cancer through a single blood test, without requiring a tissue biopsy for the initial detection, said Ramesh Hariharan, CEO of Strand Life Sciences, who is one of the authors of the study. The study examined how DNA released by different cells in the body influences the detection of cancer. An important finding was that higher levels of circulating DNA were associated with stronger cancer-related signals and better detection sensitivity, even among patients at the same stage of cancer. Researchers had expected that the increased release of DNA from immune cells in cancer patients would dilute the tumour-derived DNA signals, making cancer detection more difficult. However, the study found the opposite. The findings suggest that DNA released by tumour cells and immune cells increases together in cancer patients, helping strengthen the cancer-related signals in the blood. This provides new insights into the interaction between tumours and the immune system and its role in blood-based cancer detection, explained Mr. Hariharan, who is also an Adjunct Professor at the Indian Institute of Science, Bengaluru. CancerSpot was evaluated in newly diagnosed patients with 14 types of cancer and healthy individuals. In an independent validation cohort, it detected 72% of patients with cancer, with a false-positive rate of 1.4%.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: A low false-positive rate is important in cancer screening, as it can help reduce unnecessary follow-up investigations and invasive procedures among healthy individuals.

articles.summary: 1. Core Context & Background: CancerSpot test records 72% detection rate and 1.4% false positives; the test aims to detect multiple types of cancer through a single blood test, without requiring a tissue biopsy for the initial detection
articles.keyPoints:
• 1. Core Context & Background: CancerSpot test records 72% detection rate and 1.4% false positives; the test aims to detect multiple types of cancer through a single blood test, without requiring a tissue biopsy for the initial detection
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A blood test that looks for cancer-related changes in DNA has shown the potential to detect multiple types of cancer. In a study, the test detected 72% of cancer cases, with a false-positive rate of 1.4%. The blood test, CancerSpot, developed by Bengaluru-based Strand Life Sciences, uses DNA sequencing and Artificial Intelligence (AI) to identify changes in DNA that can indicate the presence of cancer. The research, involving 1,480 participants and 43 hospitals across India, including five in Karnataka, was conducted over four years as part of the development and clinical validation of the test. The findings have been published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences (PNAS) , a peer-reviewed scientific journal. Cells in the body release small fragments of DNA into the bloodstream. These are known as circulating or cell-free DNA. In people with cancer, some of these fragments originate from tumour cells and carry changes that can help identify the disease. CancerSpot combines DNA sequencing with AI-based analysis to examine patterns of DNA methylation. Methylation refers to chemical modifications of DNA that influence how genes function. These patterns differ between cancer cells and normal cells and can be used to identify cancer-associated signals in a blood sample. By analysing these patterns, the test aims to detect multiple types of cancer through a single blood test, without requiring a tissue biopsy for the initial detection, said Ramesh Hariharan, CEO of Strand Life Sciences, who is one of the authors of the study. The study examined how DNA released by different cells in the body influences the detection of cancer. An important finding was that higher levels of circulating DNA were associated with stronger cancer-related signals and better detection sensitivity, even among patients at the same stage of cancer. Researchers had expected that the increased release of DNA from immune cells in cancer patients would dilute the tumour-derived DNA signals, making cancer detection more difficult. However, the study found the opposite. The findings suggest that DNA released by tumour cells and immune cells increases together in cancer patients, helping strengthen the cancer-related signals in the blood. This provides new insights into the interaction between tumours and the immune system and its role in blood-based cancer detection, explained Mr. Hariharan, who is also an Adjunct Professor at the Indian Institute of Science, Bengaluru. CancerSpot was evaluated in newly diagnosed patients with 14 types of cancer and healthy individuals. In an independent validation cohort, it detected 72% of patients with cancer, with a false-positive rate of 1.4%.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: A low false-positive rate is important in cancer screening, as it can help reduce unnecessary follow-up investigations and invasive procedures among healthy individuals.

articles.title: India’s Oct. crude import bill soars 87.5% to $19.5-bn amid West Asia tensions, volumes up 11%
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: While higher petroleum product exports offer a partial natural hedge, sustained increases in crude and gas prices could intensify pressure on the country’s import bill.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: India’s crude oil import bill surged 87.5% year-on-year (YoY) to $19.5 billion in October, as elevated international benchmark prices, fuelled by renewed tensions in West Asia, sharply increased procurement costs. The increase came alongside an 11% rise in import volumes. The net import bill, calculated as imports of crude oil, petroleum products and natural gas less exports of petroleum products, rose 60% to $16 billion during the month, compared with $10 billion in October last year. Higher export realisations from petroleum products, however, provided some cushion against the escalating import burden. According to provisional data released by the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC), India imported 23.3 million metric tonnes (MMT) of crude oil in October, against 21 MMT in the corresponding month last year. The expenditure on crude imports, meanwhile, climbed to $19.5 billion from $10.4 billion, reflecting the disproportionate impact of higher international prices on the country’s energy import bill. The Indian crude oil basket averaged $119.91 per barrel in October, compared with $124.77 per barrel for Brent crude. In September, the Indian basket had averaged $116.09 per barrel, while Brent stood at $116.77 per barrel. The sustained increase in benchmark prices, amid continuing geopolitical uncertainties in West Asia, has left India exposed to higher energy procurement costs, given its dependence on imported crude oil. The impact of the rising crude import bill was partly offset by stronger earnings from petroleum product exports. India’s petroleum product exports increased 5.9% in volume terms to 5.4 MMT in October. However, export revenues surged approximately 91% to $6.3 billion.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The increase in export earnings provided an important buffer against the higher cost of crude procurement.

📈 Economic, Banking & Finance Paragraph #17 of 30 (18 NOV)

📰 India’s Oct. crude import bill soars 87.5% to $19.5-bn amid West Asia tensions, volumes up 11%

📌 Published: 18 Nov 2026, 10:23:00 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: While higher petroleum product exports offer a partial natural hedge, sustained increases in crude and gas prices could intensify pressure on the country’s import bill.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: India’s crude oil import bill surged 87.5% year-on-year (YoY) to $19.5 billion in October, as elevated international benchmark prices, fuelled by renewed tensions in West Asia, sharply increased procurement costs. The increase came alongside an 11% rise in import volumes. The net import bill, calculated as imports of crude oil, petroleum products and natural gas less exports of petroleum products, rose 60% to $16 billion during the month, compared with $10 billion in October last year. Higher export realisations from petroleum products, however, provided some cushion against the escalating import burden. According to provisional data released by the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC), India imported 23.3 million metric tonnes (MMT) of crude oil in October, against 21 MMT in the corresponding month last year. The expenditure on crude imports, meanwhile, climbed to $19.5 billion from $10.4 billion, reflecting the disproportionate impact of higher international prices on the country’s energy import bill. The Indian crude oil basket averaged $119.91 per barrel in October, compared with $124.77 per barrel for Brent crude. In September, the Indian basket had averaged $116.09 per barrel, while Brent stood at $116.77 per barrel. The sustained increase in benchmark prices, amid continuing geopolitical uncertainties in West Asia, has left India exposed to higher energy procurement costs, given its dependence on imported crude oil. The impact of the rising crude import bill was partly offset by stronger earnings from petroleum product exports. India’s petroleum product exports increased 5.9% in volume terms to 5.4 MMT in October. However, export revenues surged approximately 91% to $6.3 billion.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The increase in export earnings provided an important buffer against the higher cost of crude procurement.

articles.title: GVMC gears up for Cyclone Akvan; 11 control rooms, 55 rehabilitation centres readied
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: With Cyclone Akvan approaching, the Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation (GVMC) has sounded an alert and put its entire civic machinery on standby to tackle any eventuality arising from heavy rainfall and strong winds. The civic body has put in place extensive arrangements for emergency response, rescue, relief and restoration operations to minimise inconvenience to the public.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: GVMC Additional Commissioner S.S. Varma said that 11 control rooms had been established across the city to provide round-the-clock emergency services and respond to public complaints. Special personnel had been deployed in three shifts at the City Operations Centre (COC) at the GVMC headquarters to receive complaints and coordinate immediate relief measures. Residents can contact the GVMC control room at 180042500009 or send their complaints and requests for assistance through WhatsApp at 9014218870. As many as 55 low-lying areas across the city have been identified as vulnerable, and special monitoring arrangements have been made in these locations. The civic body has also kept 55 rehabilitation centres ready to accommodate residents who may have to be evacuated to safer locations depending on the situation. Mr. Varma appealed to people living in low-lying and hilly areas to remain vigilant and follow the instructions issued by the authorities. Residents were advised to move to safer places whenever required and remain cautious until the impact of the cyclone subsided. The GVMC has also kept a substantial fleet of machinery and vehicles ready to deal with emergencies such as fallen trees, waterlogging and road obstructions. The equipment available for relief and restoration operations includes 30 JCBs, 70 tippers, 30 mini excavators and 10 oil engines. In addition, 15 special teams have been constituted under the Horticulture Department to clear uprooted trees and branches from roads. Each team comprises a tipper, two power saws and four personnel. The teams have been strategically deployed across the Madhurawada, East, South, North, West, Gajuwaka and Pendurthi areas to ensure a quick response. For sanitation management and emergency operations, the civic body has constituted 98 Rapid Response Teams, one for each of the city’s 98 wards. Each team comprises 15 personnel and will take up the removal of stagnant rainwater, sanitation works and other emergency activities during and after the cyclone. The GVMC has also identified eight vulnerable electricity poles and is coordinating with officials of the concerned electricity department to take necessary preventive measures.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Stating that coordinated efforts were being made to tackle any eventuality, the Additional Commissioner said the GVMC was working in close coordination with the District Revenue Administration, APEPDCL and the Fire Services Department. Joint arrangements had been made to respond promptly to power supply disruptions, fallen trees and road blockages.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #7 of 30 (18 NOV)

📰 GVMC gears up for Cyclone Akvan; 11 control rooms, 55 rehabilitation centres readied

📌 Published: 18 Nov 2026, 11:27:26 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: With Cyclone Akvan approaching, the Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation (GVMC) has sounded an alert and put its entire civic machinery on standby to tackle any eventuality arising from heavy rainfall and strong winds. The civic body has put in place extensive arrangements for emergency response, rescue, relief and restoration operations to minimise inconvenience to the public.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: GVMC Additional Commissioner S.S. Varma said that 11 control rooms had been established across the city to provide round-the-clock emergency services and respond to public complaints. Special personnel had been deployed in three shifts at the City Operations Centre (COC) at the GVMC headquarters to receive complaints and coordinate immediate relief measures. Residents can contact the GVMC control room at 180042500009 or send their complaints and requests for assistance through WhatsApp at 9014218870. As many as 55 low-lying areas across the city have been identified as vulnerable, and special monitoring arrangements have been made in these locations. The civic body has also kept 55 rehabilitation centres ready to accommodate residents who may have to be evacuated to safer locations depending on the situation. Mr. Varma appealed to people living in low-lying and hilly areas to remain vigilant and follow the instructions issued by the authorities. Residents were advised to move to safer places whenever required and remain cautious until the impact of the cyclone subsided. The GVMC has also kept a substantial fleet of machinery and vehicles ready to deal with emergencies such as fallen trees, waterlogging and road obstructions. The equipment available for relief and restoration operations includes 30 JCBs, 70 tippers, 30 mini excavators and 10 oil engines. In addition, 15 special teams have been constituted under the Horticulture Department to clear uprooted trees and branches from roads. Each team comprises a tipper, two power saws and four personnel. The teams have been strategically deployed across the Madhurawada, East, South, North, West, Gajuwaka and Pendurthi areas to ensure a quick response. For sanitation management and emergency operations, the civic body has constituted 98 Rapid Response Teams, one for each of the city’s 98 wards. Each team comprises 15 personnel and will take up the removal of stagnant rainwater, sanitation works and other emergency activities during and after the cyclone. The GVMC has also identified eight vulnerable electricity poles and is coordinating with officials of the concerned electricity department to take necessary preventive measures.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Stating that coordinated efforts were being made to tackle any eventuality, the Additional Commissioner said the GVMC was working in close coordination with the District Revenue Administration, APEPDCL and the Fire Services Department. Joint arrangements had been made to respond promptly to power supply disruptions, fallen trees and road blockages.

संवैधानिक — देश के संविधान (Constitution) के दायरे और मौलिक अधिकारों के अनुरूप।

✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial

महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Administration' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Inconvenience (Adjective / Verb)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Inconvenience' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Restrictive, Counteractive, Adverse  |  ✖ Ant: Constructive, Supportive, Favorable

Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "GVMC gears up for Cyclone Akvan; 11 control rooms, 55 rehabilitation centres readied", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. With Cyclone Akvan approaching, the Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation (GVMC) has sounded an alert and put its entire civic machinery on...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'GVMC gears up for Cyclone Akvan; 11 control room' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'GVMC gears up for Cyclone Akvan; 11 control r' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'GVMC gears up for Cyclone Akvan; 11 control r' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "With Cyclone Akvan approaching, the Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation (GVMC) has sounded an alert and put its entire civic machinery on..." (Hinglish Arth: चक्रवात अकवन के करीब आने के साथ, ग्रेटर विशाखापत्तनम नगर निगम (जीवीएमसी) ने अलर्ट जारी कर दिया है और भारी बारिश और तेज बारिश से उत्पन्न होने वाली किसी भी स्थिति से निपटने के लिए अपनी पूरी नागरिक मशीनरी को तैयार रखा है।)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "GVMC gears up for Cyclone Akvan; 11 control rooms, 55 rehabilitation centres readied"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. Joint arrangements had been made to respond promptly to power supply disruptions, fallen trees and road blockages.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "Joint arrangements had been made to respond promptly to power supply disruptions, fallen trees and road blockages." (Hinglish Arth: बिजली आपूर्ति में व्यवधान, गिरे हुए पेड़ और सड़क अवरोधों पर तुरंत प्रतिक्रिया देने के लिए संयुक्त व्यवस्था की गई थी।)

articles.title: Keralam govt. issues order renaming mental health centres despite protests by psychiatrists, doctors
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: GO issued renaming Mental Health Centres as “Regional Institutes of Happiness and Wellness

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Keralam government has gone ahead with its decision to rename the Mental Health Centres (MHCs) in the State as “Regional Institutes of Happiness and Wellness”, even after the pitfalls of such a move was pointed out by psychiatry professionals and other professional bodies of doctors. With the government issuing the government order (GO) on November 13, formalising the change in nomenclature, the Indian Psychiatric Society’s (IPS) Keralam branch and other medical bodies, including the Indian Medical Association (IMA) and the Kerala Government Medical Officers’ Association, have renewed their warning that the change in nomenclature could undermine the clinical, academic and legal identity of the State’s MHCs. Mental health professionals in the State have yet again pointed out to the government that the nomenclature, Regional Institutes of Happiness and Wellness, was one that trivialised the legitimacy and seriousness of a branch of modern medicine which dealt with the treatment of serious mental health disorders. The controversy follows a suggestion by a Division Bench of the Kerala High Court on August 21, 2026, that the government consider renaming the centres to address the stigma associated with them. The court had suggested the name “Institutes of Behavioural Management”. With the IMA and the IPS Kerala approaching the High Court with their objections, the court had asked the government to hold consultations with the medical professionals on the issues they had brought up. Accordingly, the Keralam branch of the Indian Psychiatric Society and the IMA had met the Health department officials, including the Principal Secretary (Health), on September 16 and had proposed “Regional Institutes of Psychiatry and Behavioural Sciences” as the best option if the government was keen on renaming the MHCs. However, despite the concerns expressed by the medical professionals about the repercussions of renaming medical institutions to resemble the names of spas or the so-called holistic treatment centres that are a dime a dozen in the State, the government was apparently unwilling to drop the ‘happiness and wellness' tag, and chose to rename MHCs as Regional Institutes of Happiness and Wellness. The psychiatrists have urged the government to reconsider the decision, arguing that replacing the established terms “mental health” and “psychiatry” with “happiness and wellness” would neither address the stigma associated with mental illness nor reflect the specialised treatment provided by these institutions. They have pointed out that happiness and wellness are broad concepts that do not adequately convey the purpose of a specialised psychiatric treatment facility.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: In a statement issued on November 17, the IPS pointed out that the Mental Healthcare Act, 2017, and the statutory bodies established under it use the term “mental health.”

The psychiatrists have urged the government to reconsider the decision, arguing that replacing the established terms “mental health” and “psychiatry” with “happiness and wellness” would neither address the stigma associated with mental illness nor reflect the specialised treatment provided by these institutions. They have pointed out that happiness and wellness are broad concepts that do not adequately convey the purpose of a specialised psychiatric treatment facility.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: In a statement issued on November 17, the IPS pointed out that the Mental Healthcare Act, 2017, and the statutory bodies established under it use the term “mental health.”

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #8 of 30 (18 NOV)

📰 Keralam govt. issues order renaming mental health centres despite protests by psychiatrists, doctors

📌 Published: 18 Nov 2026, 11:14:20 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: GO issued renaming Mental Health Centres as “Regional Institutes of Happiness and Wellness

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Keralam government has gone ahead with its decision to rename the Mental Health Centres (MHCs) in the State as “Regional Institutes of Happiness and Wellness”, even after the pitfalls of such a move was pointed out by psychiatry professionals and other professional bodies of doctors. With the government issuing the government order (GO) on November 13, formalising the change in nomenclature, the Indian Psychiatric Society’s (IPS) Keralam branch and other medical bodies, including the Indian Medical Association (IMA) and the Kerala Government Medical Officers’ Association, have renewed their warning that the change in nomenclature could undermine the clinical, academic and legal identity of the State’s MHCs. Mental health professionals in the State have yet again pointed out to the government that the nomenclature, Regional Institutes of Happiness and Wellness, was one that trivialised the legitimacy and seriousness of a branch of modern medicine which dealt with the treatment of serious mental health disorders. The controversy follows a suggestion by a Division Bench of the Kerala High Court on August 21, 2026, that the government consider renaming the centres to address the stigma associated with them. The court had suggested the name “Institutes of Behavioural Management”. With the IMA and the IPS Kerala approaching the High Court with their objections, the court had asked the government to hold consultations with the medical professionals on the issues they had brought up. Accordingly, the Keralam branch of the Indian Psychiatric Society and the IMA had met the Health department officials, including the Principal Secretary (Health), on September 16 and had proposed “Regional Institutes of Psychiatry and Behavioural Sciences” as the best option if the government was keen on renaming the MHCs. However, despite the concerns expressed by the medical professionals about the repercussions of renaming medical institutions to resemble the names of spas or the so-called holistic treatment centres that are a dime a dozen in the State, the government was apparently unwilling to drop the ‘happiness and wellness' tag, and chose to rename MHCs as Regional Institutes of Happiness and Wellness. The psychiatrists have urged the government to reconsider the decision, arguing that replacing the established terms “mental health” and “psychiatry” with “happiness and wellness” would neither address the stigma associated with mental illness nor reflect the specialised treatment provided by these institutions. They have pointed out that happiness and wellness are broad concepts that do not adequately convey the purpose of a specialised psychiatric treatment facility.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: In a statement issued on November 17, the IPS pointed out that the Mental Healthcare Act, 2017, and the statutory bodies established under it use the term “mental health.”

articles.title: Bihar doctor fined ₹30 lakh for leaving surgical gauze in abdomen during gallbladder surgery
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The Bihar State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission found the doctor guilty of gross medical negligence The case is related to the late Nibha Singh, a resident of Madhepura, Bihar.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Bihar State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) ordered a doctor, found guilty of gross negligence for leaving a surgical gauze (cotton pad) inside a patient’s abdomen during a routine gallbladder operation, to pay a compensation of ₹30 lakh. The case is related to the late Nibha Singh (aged 53), wife of Mani Kant Singh, a resident of Madhepura, Bihar. Following complaints of abdominal pain, the deceased had consulted Dr. Rajesh Kumar Singh (Opposite Party No. 1), a laparoscopic surgeon at Gayatri Nursing Home in Saharsa. Acting on the doctor’s advice, she underwent surgery to remove her gallbladder on March 19, 2016. Post-surgery, her health began to deteriorate rapidly; she suffered from severe abdominal pain, vomiting, and a bowel obstruction. Although she was examined by several doctors and hospitals, the root cause of her condition remained unidentified. Then she was admitted to the Sir Ganga Ram Hospital in New Delhi where doctors performed an emergency surgery (laparotomy). During the procedure, a large, blood-soaked surgical gauze (sponge) measuring 15x4x3 cm—was discovered inside her abdomen, which had caused an infection (peritonitis) to spread throughout the abdominal cavity. Despite medical intervention, the patient passed away on July 1, 2016 — just hours after being discharged from the hospital — due to severe complications and the resulting infection. The bench included the President Justice Sanjay Kumar and Judicial Member Md Shamim Akhtar. Mr. Akhtar, cited previous rulings by the Supreme Court and the National Commission, clarified that leaving surgical materials or gauze inside a patient’s abdomen during an operation clearly falls under the category of ‘gross negligence.’ In its order, the Commission stated that it is the primary duty of a doctor and their surgical team to account for all surgical instruments and gauze before closing the incision; failure to do so in this instance put the patient’s life at grave risk. The Commission has directed the primary erring doctor (Opposite Party No. 1) to pay the aggrieved husband a sum of ₹30,00,000 (thirty lakh rupees) as compensation, along with ₹20,000 towards litigation costs, within 60 days of receiving the order.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “Should the payment not be made within the stipulated timeframe, it will accrue interest at a rate of 8% per annum. Opposite party no.1 failed to act upon the repeated visit of patient with complain of severe abdomen pain and distention and should have prompted timely investigation using appropriate imaging modalities instead opposite party no.1 advised symptomatic medicines and failed to diagnose real cause of pain and suffering,“ the Commission observed in the order.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #9 of 30 (18 NOV)

📰 Bihar doctor fined ₹30 lakh for leaving surgical gauze in abdomen during gallbladder surgery

📌 Published: 18 Nov 2026, 11:06:36 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The Bihar State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission found the doctor guilty of gross medical negligence The case is related to the late Nibha Singh, a resident of Madhepura, Bihar.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Bihar State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) ordered a doctor, found guilty of gross negligence for leaving a surgical gauze (cotton pad) inside a patient’s abdomen during a routine gallbladder operation, to pay a compensation of ₹30 lakh. The case is related to the late Nibha Singh (aged 53), wife of Mani Kant Singh, a resident of Madhepura, Bihar. Following complaints of abdominal pain, the deceased had consulted Dr. Rajesh Kumar Singh (Opposite Party No. 1), a laparoscopic surgeon at Gayatri Nursing Home in Saharsa. Acting on the doctor’s advice, she underwent surgery to remove her gallbladder on March 19, 2016. Post-surgery, her health began to deteriorate rapidly; she suffered from severe abdominal pain, vomiting, and a bowel obstruction. Although she was examined by several doctors and hospitals, the root cause of her condition remained unidentified. Then she was admitted to the Sir Ganga Ram Hospital in New Delhi where doctors performed an emergency surgery (laparotomy). During the procedure, a large, blood-soaked surgical gauze (sponge) measuring 15x4x3 cm—was discovered inside her abdomen, which had caused an infection (peritonitis) to spread throughout the abdominal cavity. Despite medical intervention, the patient passed away on July 1, 2016 — just hours after being discharged from the hospital — due to severe complications and the resulting infection. The bench included the President Justice Sanjay Kumar and Judicial Member Md Shamim Akhtar. Mr. Akhtar, cited previous rulings by the Supreme Court and the National Commission, clarified that leaving surgical materials or gauze inside a patient’s abdomen during an operation clearly falls under the category of ‘gross negligence.’ In its order, the Commission stated that it is the primary duty of a doctor and their surgical team to account for all surgical instruments and gauze before closing the incision; failure to do so in this instance put the patient’s life at grave risk. The Commission has directed the primary erring doctor (Opposite Party No. 1) to pay the aggrieved husband a sum of ₹30,00,000 (thirty lakh rupees) as compensation, along with ₹20,000 towards litigation costs, within 60 days of receiving the order.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “Should the payment not be made within the stipulated timeframe, it will accrue interest at a rate of 8% per annum. Opposite party no.1 failed to act upon the repeated visit of patient with complain of severe abdomen pain and distention and should have prompted timely investigation using appropriate imaging modalities instead opposite party no.1 advised symptomatic medicines and failed to diagnose real cause of pain and suffering,“ the Commission observed in the order.

Accountability (Noun)
जवाबदेही — अपने फैसलों और काम का जनता तथा संविधान को हिसाब देने की बाध्यता।

महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Investigation' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Restrictive, Counteractive, Adverse  |  ✖ Ant: Constructive, Supportive, Favorable
Compensation (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Compensation' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Laparoscopic (Adjective)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Laparoscopic' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "Bihar doctor fined ₹30 lakh for leaving surgical gauze in abdomen during gallbladder surgery", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. The Bihar State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission found the doctor guilty of gross medical negligence The case is related to the late Nibha...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Bihar doctor fined ₹30 lakh for leaving surgical' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Bihar doctor fined ₹30 lakh for leaving surgi' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Bihar doctor fined ₹30 lakh for leaving surgi' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "The Bihar State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission found the doctor guilty of gross medical negligence The case is related to the late Nibha..." (Hinglish Arth: बिहार राज्य उपभोक्ता विवाद निवारण आयोग ने डॉक्टर को घोर चिकित्सीय लापरवाही का दोषी पाया। यह मामला बिहार के मधेपुरा की रहने वाली दिवंगत निभा सिंह से जुड़ा है।)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Bihar doctor fined ₹30 lakh for leaving surgical gauze in abdomen during gallbladder surgery"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. Opposite party no.1 failed to act upon the repeated visit of patient with complain of severe abdomen pain and distention and should have prompted...
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "Opposite party no.1 failed to act upon the repeated visit of patient with complain of severe abdomen pain and distention and should have prompted..." (Hinglish Arth: विपक्षी पार्टी नंबर 1 गंभीर पेट दर्द और फैलाव की शिकायत के साथ रोगी के बार-बार आने पर कार्रवाई करने में विफल रही और इसके विपरीत, उचित इमेजिंग तौर-तरीकों का उपयोग करके समय पर जांच की जानी चाहिए थी।)

articles.title: HC interim orders over fertility centres
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Justice N.V. Shravan Kumar of the Telangana High Court on Wednesday directed the officials of the Medical and Health department to shift the persons under treatment at Oasis Fertility centres to IVF centres of the government. The ongoing medical treatment to those 51 persons should be continued at the government IVF centres, the judge said.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The judge passed the interim direction after hearing a writ petition filed by the Oasis Fertility centres being operated by the Sadguru Health Care Services Private Limited questioning the recent cases initiated by police accusing fertility centres of indulging in artificial insemination. The petitioner’s counsel contended that his client did not indulge in any illegal activity. The medical treatment being extended to 51 persons in the fertility centres was at different stages. If adequate precautions were not taken, the objectives of the treatment would be defeated, the counsel said. The judge instructed the government to file counter affidavits within two weeks.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: In a related development, Justice T. Madhavi Devi of the HC issued notices to the government in a writ petition filed by doctor Durga Rao who was facing charges of collecting sperm samples illegally. The doctor challenged the registration of multiple cases on similar charges against him. The matter was adjourned to November 23 for next hearing.

articles.title: Higher pension to 4.45 lakh applicants may cost EPFO ₹1.1 lakh crore
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: As on November 13, demand letters were issued to 4,45,471 applicants and pension payment orders have been issued to 1,51,874 pensioners

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Four years after a Supreme Court judgement on provident fund pension based on higher wages, the Employees Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) has said that it may have to spend an additional ₹1.109 lakh crore to implement the order and pay higher pensions to about 4.45 lakh applicants. In a communication to the Central Board of Trustees, which is meeting here on Thursday, the EPFO said it considered 15.24 lakh applications for higher pension and, as on November 13, demand letters were issued to 4,45,471 applicants and pension payment orders (PPOs) have been issued to 1,51,874 pensioners. The EPFO received 17.49 lakh applications for pension on higher wages after the Supreme Court judgment, of which 2.24 lakh applications were not forwarded by the employers till the last date of January 31, 2025. Out of around 15.24 lakh applications received by the EPFO, 99.2 per cent have been disposed of and 4,45,471 demand letters have been issued. Out of these, 80,067 cases have been found ineligible later due to non-remittance of demand amount. “Around 2,62,102 applicants have deposited the demand amount/ consent out of which 1,03,793 are continuing in service and 1,58,309 have already retired. Out of these applicants, 1,53,901 have submitted Form-10D or are already pensioners. PPOs have been issued to a total of around 1,51,874 applicants. In addition, 2,027 PPOs are under finalisation and will be issued very shortly,” the EPFO said in the communication to its trustees. The total additional liability is ₹78,501.42 crore for 3,15,601 applications. “The per-person liability is estimated at ₹25.99 lakh for active members and ₹23.14 lakh for pensioners, resulting in an overall average per-person liability of around ₹24.9 lakh across both groups,” the EPFO said. It added that till November 13, demand amount or consent has been received from 2,62,102 applicants to the joint option for which the additional proportionate liability would be approximately ₹65,263 crore. “Similarly, the estimated additional proportionate liability considering approval of 100 per cent of total applications for which demand notices have been issued (i.e., 4.454 lakh) would be about ₹1.109 lakh crore. This estimation, however, is likely to vary in case any additional set of employees, members, pensioners become eligible for any reason whatsoever, in future, particularly on account of the ongoing litigations,” the EPFO said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: To resolve the delays, the EPFO has said timely Issue of PPOs and release of arrears will be implemented and all legal cases will be defended properly to ensure that there is no adverse legal consequence. It has urged the CBT to take note of the information and give directions to the EPFO on the matter.

In a communication to the Central Board of Trustees, which is meeting here on Thursday, the EPFO said it considered 15.24 lakh applications for higher pension and, as on November 13, demand letters were issued to 4,45,471 applicants and pension payment orders (PPOs) have been issued to 1,51,874 pensioners. The EPFO received 17.49 lakh applications for pension on higher wages after the Supreme Court judgment, of which 2.24 lakh applications were not forwarded by the employers till the last date of January 31, 2025. Out of around 15.24 lakh applications received by the EPFO, 99.2 per cent have been disposed of and 4,45,471 demand letters have been issued. Out of these, 80,067 cases have been found ineligible later due to non-remittance of demand amount. “Around 2,62,102 applicants have deposited the demand amount/ consent out of which 1,03,793 are continuing in service and 1,58,309 have already retired. Out of these applicants, 1,53,901 have submitted Form-10D or are already pensioners. PPOs have been issued to a total of around 1,51,874 applicants. In addition, 2,027 PPOs are under finalisation and will be issued very shortly,” the EPFO said in the communication to its trustees. The total additional liability is ₹78,501.42 crore for 3,15,601 applications. “The per-person liability is estimated at ₹25.99 lakh for active members and ₹23.14 lakh for pensioners, resulting in an overall average per-person liability of around ₹24.9 lakh across both groups,” the EPFO said. It added that till November 13, demand amount or consent has been received from 2,62,102 applicants to the joint option for which the additional proportionate liability would be approximately ₹65,263 crore. “Similarly, the estimated additional proportionate liability considering approval of 100 per cent of total applications for which demand notices have been issued (i.e., 4.454 lakh) would be about ₹1.109 lakh crore. This estimation, however, is likely to vary in case any additional set of employees, members, pensioners become eligible for any reason whatsoever, in future, particularly on account of the ongoing litigations,” the EPFO said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: To resolve the delays, the EPFO has said timely Issue of PPOs and release of arrears will be implemented and all legal cases will be defended properly to ensure that there is no adverse legal consequence. It has urged the CBT to take note of the information and give directions to the EPFO on the matter.
